title: What's Hidden Matters: Identifying Planning-Critical Occluded Agents using Vision-Language Models
relevance_note: HIGH — ranks occluded agents by their impact on the ego plan (Planning KL-divergence), i.e. relevance defined by plan change, for occlusion hazards like the project's.
what: Uses Planning KL-divergence to rank occluded agents by impact on the ego plan, has GPT-5 write structured annotations, and builds a nuScenes benchmark of high-impact scenarios. Fine-tuned smaller VLMs beat larger zero-shot ones; PKL-guided data selection improves about 30% over random sampling.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (plan-conditioned relevance of hidden objects as ground truth or feature for the occlusion hazard). Not query selection.

title: SimpleVSF: VLM-Scoring Fusion for Trajectory Prediction of End-to-End Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — a VLM picks the final trajectory from the per-scorer top-ranked candidates; direct example of a VLM trajectory selector.
what: Combines conventional scorers and VLM-enhanced scorers with a weight fusioner (quantitative) and a VLM-based fusioner (qualitative). The VLM module is Qwen2-VL-2B fine-tuned on navtrain to generate cognitive directives (html text). Reported as leading approach in the ICCV 2025 NAVSIM v2 challenge.
thesis_use: ranker-side related work (VLM over a candidate set).

title: OmniDrive-R1: Reinforcement-driven Interleaved Multi-modal Chain-of-Thought for Trustworthy Vision-Language Autonomous Driving
venue: CVPR Workshops 2026 (OpenAlex DOI 10.1109/cvprf71909.2026.00111; not confirmed on a venue page)
relevance_note: HIGH — "thinking with images" for driving: the model chooses between text reasoning, zoom-in on a region, or answering.
what: Interleaved multimodal CoT with a zoom action; two-stage RL with Clip-GRPO, an annotation-free grounding reward that avoids external tool-call instability. On DriveLMM-o1, Qwen2.5-VL-7B goes 51.77 -> 80.35 reasoning score and 37.81 -> 73.62 answer accuracy (abstract). Future work lists lane and depth tools (from a search summary, not verified).
thesis_use: competitor for the ROI tool; evidence that zoom helps VQA-style driving. No planning, no budget curve.

title: ToolGate: Token-Efficient Pre-Call Control for Tool-Augmented Vision-Language Agents
relevance_note: HIGH — learned execute/skip controller for perceptual tool calls; finds most tool calls do not change the immediate answer (helpful 11.8% vs harmful 9.9% calls in the baseline).
what: A ReAct VLM agent proposes a perceptual tool call (OCR, detection, segmentation); a lightweight external controller on trajectory text and structural features (no pixels, no hidden states) predicts execute or skip. Across five benchmarks the baseline's helpful and harmful calls occur at similar rates (11.8% vs 9.9%) and 78.3% of calls leave the forced-answer argmax unchanged (Qwen3-VL-30B, 15,782 labeled calls). ToolGate cuts token cost to 64-69% of unrestricted ReAct at preserved cross-domain accuracy; executed calls fall 2.73 to 1.02 per episode. Labels are a proxy built from forced-answer probes before/after the call; the paper says it does not estimate true counterfactual VoI.
thesis_use: baseline / evidence that naive agents over-call tools; abstain-on-tool analog; not driving, not candidate-aware.

title: When Should a VLM Look? Paying Only for Visual Calls That Were Needed and Used
relevance_note: HIGH (method) — decision value ("realized visual branch vs answering immediately") plus evidence value ("crop vs random same-size patches") per call, i.e. a counterfactual value-of-call label.
what: CounterCredit pays only calls that were both needed and used. Only 10-12% of calls on the cold-start checkpoint were needed and used, and released agents make spurious calls 36-87% of the time. Reaches 89.5% V*, 80.2% HR-Bench-4K, 76.4% HR-Bench-8K, +6.3 to 9.4 over outcome GRPO at 1.78 vs 1.84 calls per question (abstract). Not driving.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (expected-gain label, spurious-call metric). Supports the project's finding that the VLM's tool choice is poor.

title: Learning to Evaluate Perception Models Using Planner-Centric Metrics
relevance_note: HIGH - defines perception quality by the effect of its output on the downstream driving plan (PKL), the root of our 'decision-relevant' notion.
what: Proposes a metric for 3D detection that isolates detection and measures the impact the detections have on the downstream driving task, instead of treating all errors equally. The abstract says it penalizes mistakes that other metrics miss without being hand-designed to. Already cited in raw/B; the 2026 occluded-agent paper in papers.csv builds on it.
thesis_use: Cite as the origin of plan-conditioned relevance. Borrow: a KL-on-plan score as an alternative oracle gain label for each tool. Contrast: PKL scores a fixed perception output, we choose which query to make.

title: Safe Occlusion-aware Autonomous Driving via Game-Theoretic Active Perception
relevance_note: HIGH - occlusion hazard plus planning that accounts for what future observations will reveal, i.e. active perception inside the planner.
what: Abstract: poses safe planning under occlusion as a hybrid zero-sum dynamic game between the AV (evader) and an initially hidden traffic participant (pursuer); gives worst-case safety guarantees while accounting for the vehicle's ability to avoid road users once detected; demonstrated in CARLA urban and highway scenarios.
thesis_use: classic active-perception-for-driving reference.

title: Robots That Ask For Help: Uncertainty Alignment for Large Language Model Planners
venue: CoRL 2023 (PMLR v229, ren23a; from search listing)
relevance_note: HIGH - conformal prediction decides when an LLM planner asks for help, minimizing help calls; the closest older 'when to ask' method.
what: Verified in the html: the LLM planner is cast as multiple-choice QA over generated candidate options; conformal prediction on next-token likelihoods from a calibration set yields a reduced prediction set; "The LLM is certain if this prediction set is a singleton, and triggers help from a human otherwise." Intro/conclusion: "reducing human help by 10-24% compared to baseline approaches that lack formal assurances". Guarantee assumes the true option is in the set when help is accurate (task-completion level 1-epsilon, with 1-delta=0.99 over calibration sampling). Stated limitation: it does not yet model perception-module uncertainty.
thesis_use: comparison. KnowNo's trigger is candidate-conditioned, like the project's, but it measures the planner's confidence over WHICH candidate is right (output-likelihood ambiguity), asks a human who resolves everything, and has one action ("ask"). The project's selector instead reads how the candidates DIVERGE geometrically, chooses WHICH of several tools to call, and is trained on the measured gain of each tool (noisy outcome), so it can learn that ambiguity is not resolvable by any available tool and abstain. KnowNo's set-size rule is the natural "candidate-ambiguity trigger" baseline for the Pareto plot (call if the ranker's conformal set over K candidates has size > 1), and its coverage guarantee is the template for the future CRC phase.

title: Object Importance Estimation using Counterfactual Reasoning for Intelligent Driving
relevance_note: HIGH - object importance defined by how perturbing an object's motion changes the ego's driving, a counterfactual decision-relevance label.
what: Introduces HOIST (human-annotated object importance in simulated traffic) and a counterfactual method that modifies object motion and ascribes importance by the effect on ego driving; beats baselines on HOIST.
thesis_use: idea to borrow for label construction (which hazard changes the chosen candidate).

title: AgentThink: A Unified Framework for Tool-Augmented Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
venue: Findings of EMNLP 2025 (from search result; not checked on the abs page)
relevance_note: HIGH — the driving tool-library baseline (visual, detection, prediction, occupancy, mapping tools); older than the 2025-07 window but essential and not in known_papers.
what: Builds a driving tool library, generates self-verified tool-using reasoning data, trains SFT then GRPO for autonomous tool invocation, and adds a multi-tool usage evaluation protocol. On DriveLMM-o1 it reports +53.91% reasoning score and +33.54% answer accuracy (abstract).
thesis_use: baseline family / tool-set reference; its tool-use evaluation protocol could be borrowed. Trajectory-agnostic.

title: MTRDrive: Memory-Tool Synergistic Reasoning for Robust Autonomous Driving in Corner Cases
relevance_note: HIGH — memory plus dynamic toolkit for a 3B driving VLM, evaluated on NAVSIM (planning) and a roadwork corner-case benchmark.
what: Closed loop of experience retrieval and dynamic toolkits; reports PDMS 88.3 on NAVSIM without CoT, driving metric 79.8%, planning accuracy 82.6%, and 80.2% zero-shot on the new Roadwork-VLM benchmark (abstract).
thesis_use: competitor; the only tool-using driving VLM here with a planning benchmark (NAVSIM). Roadwork-VLM is a possible hazard benchmark. Cited by the 2609.08217 line of work (that paper is its successor by theme; not confirmed same authors).

title: MindDrive: An All-in-One Framework Bridging World Models and Vision-Language Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — generate candidates with a world-action model, then a VLM-oriented evaluator (VLoE) scores them on safety, comfort, efficiency.
what: "context simulation, candidate generation, multi-objective trade-off". Claims SOTA on NAVSIM-v1 and v2 (abstract gives no numbers).
thesis_use: competitor / baseline for VLM-evaluator ranking; contrast with project's finding that prompting a VLM is weak.

title: From Representational Complementarity to Dual Systems: Synergizing VLM and Vision-Only Backbones for End-to-End Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — closest to candidate-set-conditioned gating of an expensive model: a learned trajectory scorer over a cross-model candidate set, with the VLM invoked only in some scenarios.
what: Compares VLM hidden states (InternVL3, Qwen3VL) with vision-only encoders under a fixed diffusion planner; finds VLMs help in semantically complex long-tail cases, vision encoders in simple geometry scenes. HybridDriveVLA raises NAVSIM PDMS 90.80 to 92.10 via a learned scorer; DualDriveVLA invokes the VLM in 15% of scenarios for 91.00 PDMS with about 1.9x lower latency than the VLM baseline (abstract figures; a search summary said 3.2x throughput, not verified).
thesis_use: baseline; the oracle-selector-vs-confidence-selector gap is the same shape as the project's Pareto story.

title: Look Where It Matters: High-Resolution Crops Retrieval for Efficient VLMs
relevance_note: HIGH — a VLM decides whether and where to fetch high-resolution crops by tool call, trained with SFT then multi-turn GRPO with a crop-cost penalty. Labels for "needs crop" come from a judge comparing low- vs high-resolution answers. The 80.3% vs 80.46% and 36% pixel figures came from a search summary and are UNVERIFIED (abstract has no numbers).
what: Stage 1 label (Sec. 3): run a base VLM on low- and full-resolution inputs; an LLM judge compares both to ground truth; "If it judges a_low as correct (or ties it with a_full), we label the example as no crop needed LR; otherwise ... HR". Then a grounding model gives crop boxes, SFT then multi-turn GRPO with composite reward including crop-cost penalties. Abstract: "matches full-resolution accuracy while retaining only 36% of visual tokens"; Fig. 1: 80.3% with 36% of tokens across six benchmarks.
thesis_use: precedent for deriving a binary "query needed" label by comparing outcomes with and without the extra information (single run, no averaging).

title: ASSCG: Just-Right Gating over Chattering for Fast-Slow LLM Planning in Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — learns when to query the slow system under compute cost (Query/Cache/Drop), trained with SFT then GRPO-style compute-aware RL.
what: Frame-level gate with RWKV backbone for AsyncDriver (nuPlan Hard20 67.28, +2.28, latency -60%) and a RecogDrive-based dual system on NAVSIM (91.4 PDMS, +0.6, speed +25%).
thesis_use: baseline family; budget-aware RL gate; the Cache action (reuse a previous answer) is a third option next to query/abstain.

title: Drive by Hindsight and Foresight: Tool-Grounded Synergistic Reasoning over Hierarchical Memory for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — newest DriveAgent-R1-style competitor: proactive adaptive tool invocation driven by scene state plus retrieved experience.
what: Couples a hierarchical driving memory (short-term scene state, long-term experience incl. tool strategies) with proactive tool calls in a closed reasoning loop; SFT then GRPO on multi-step teacher rollouts. Reports 80.03 overall reasoning score and 79.09% MCQ on DriveLMM-o1 for a 7B model (abstract).
thesis_use: competitor / related work; the trigger is scene-and-memory-conditioned, not candidate-conditioned. Not read beyond abstract.

title: ETM: Event Trigger Module based VLM for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — learned trigger deciding when to invoke an expensive VLM, framed as information-gain-driven and cost-balanced, trained with information-gain pseudo-labels plus corner-case labels; nuScenes.
what: Lightweight trigger policy that activates the VLM only when refreshed semantic reasoning is expected to improve planning; trained with corner-case labels plus information-gain pseudo-labels. On nuScenes keeps planning accuracy comparable to always-triggered while cutting VLM invocation from 100% to 32%, latency by nearly 50% and compute by about 64%.
thesis_use: closest "expected-gain label" precedent in driving; competitor to the scene-uncertainty baseline; differs in that it gates one VLM, not which tool, and not candidate-conditioned.

title: DriveScout: Sharpening MLLM Perception in Autonomous Driving with Adaptive and Robust Visual Focusing
relevance_note: HIGH — a DriveAgent-R1-style follow-up: RL for "selective evidence acquisition" by cropping, with Necessity-Aware Focus Optimization to cut redundant visual operations; includes a paired clear/motion-blur nuScenes VQA benchmark (SCOUT).
what: RL framework for Think-with-Images driving MLLMs; Target-Grounded Spatial Credit plus Necessity-Aware Focus Optimization and a progressive blur curriculum; introduces SCOUT, a paired nuScenes driving VQA benchmark with motion-blur variants. Improves blur robustness and reduces redundant visual operations (numbers not in abstract).
thesis_use: competitor / related work for the learned-tool-use side; its necessity reward is an alternative to expected-gain targets; sensor-degradation benchmark idea.

title: The Decision Value of Perception Compute (DEEP: Decision Evaluation for Escalated Perception)
relevance_note: HIGH — defines decision value of spending extra perception compute on an input as downstream-loss change, and benchmarks pre-escalation allocators against a budget-constrained decision oracle with selection/latency/energy budgets and allocator self-cost charged.
what: Defines decision value of perception compute as the change in downstream loss when escalating from cheap to expensive perception, and scores pre-escalation allocators against a budget-constrained decision oracle with their own compute charged. With monocular geometry on KITTI/nuScenes, 34-54% of escalations that change loss make it worse; on nuScenes perception-level gain often disagrees in sign with decision value; choosing signals by perception gain loses 7.4% of all-cheap loss. Learned allocators select nearly as much harm as random; at a 20% latency budget only routers at about 3.5% of a detector pass beat random. Also evaluated open-loop on nuPlan with PDM-Closed.
thesis_use: framing and baseline design (oracle selector, budget curves, charge the selector's own cost); evidence that uncertainty triggers can be harmful; risk that learned selectors give small gains over random.
verified: OpenReview search record (abstract, truncated at ~1600 chars) read. ; arXiv 2609.35910 abs meta fetched (main thread), html read (X1)

title: MosaicDrive: Task-Aware Multi-Camera Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — close overlap in motivation: criticizes uncertainty-triggered acquisition in tool-augmented driving agents and replaces it with task-conditioned acquisition plus verification; conditions on the question, not on candidate plans.
what: Argues the confidence that triggers retrieval of extra camera views is computed from evidence already held, so it carries no information about never-observed regions, and that extra evidence can overturn a correct prior answer. Derives camera and tool requirements from the question, uses a source-aware verifier (Arbiter) with targeted re-queries, and evaluates on MOSICQA (multi-camera driving QA with executed tool traces) with a protocol separating coverage from selectivity, correction from abstention, and answer quality from acquisition cost. No numbers in the abstract.
thesis_use: competitor / argument ally against scene-uncertainty triggering; borrow its protocol of separating coverage vs selectivity vs cost; note it is QA-based, not planner-conditioned.
verified: OpenReview search record (abstract) read; not arXiv.

title: CLARINET: Augmenting Language Models to Ask Clarification Questions for Retrieval
relevance_note: HIGH — nearest neighbour-field precedent: a learned question chooser that takes the top candidates as input and is trained on a counterfactual rank-gain target.
what: Picks which clarification question to ask so that the true item's rank rises. For each training query, candidate questions are answered by a GPT-3 user simulator; the model is trained on questions that put the target in the top 10 or raise its rank by 10. Input is the user query, past interactions and the top book candidates. It beats information gain by 17% and vanilla LLM prompting by 39% relative on retrieval success (abstract, book search). Appendix table has Random, EIG, KL and CLARINET rows.
thesis_use: must cite as prior art for candidate-conditioned query selection trained on counterfactual gain. Differences: one query type, no "none", no oracle selector, no uncertainty-trigger baseline, no hazard/noise levels.

title: Perception in Plan: Coupled Perception and Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — perception targeted by planning priors (multi-mode anchored trajectories); closest conceptual neighbour to candidate-conditioned querying, though not a budgeted tool choice.
what: VeteranAD gathers traffic elements along anchored trajectories and predicts future trajectories autoregressively while focusing on relevant regions at each step. Reports state-of-the-art on NAVSIM and Bench2Drive (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: related work (trajectory-conditioned perception inside a network, versus an explicit tool selector); idea to borrow: ROI along each candidate.

title: AdaDrive: Self-Adaptive Slow-Fast System for Language-Grounded Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — learns when to invoke an LLM in a driving stack, a "whether to call" decision; scene-conditioned, so a baseline-style comparator.
what: Slow-fast framework deciding when the LLM is activated (adaptive activation loss, comparative learning) and how strongly its output is fused with a conventional planner (continuous scaled influence from scene complexity and prediction confidence). The abstract reports state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency on language-grounded driving benchmarks; no numbers given.
thesis_use: related work / baseline family for scene-uncertainty triggering; contrast: its trigger does not see the candidate set.

title: Best-of-Evidence: Best-of-N Selection under Partial Verification
relevance_note: HIGH — fixed candidate pool plus a budget over evidence actions that can change the choice; already in papers.csv and in report section 2.
what: Only seen via a search summary this run (confirms: pool kept fixed, budget spent on evidence actions that can change the final choice, zero budget reduces to plain best-of-N). Not re-read.
thesis_use: the strongest "this is X applied to driving" candidate besides CLARINET; no training, so the learned-from-gain part differs.
verified: UNVERIFIED in this run (search summary only); see Y_leads_followup.md

title: BudgetVerify: Budget-Tiered Verification for Financial QA
relevance_note: HIGH — learned router over {no verification, cheap check, strong check}, trained on offline per-tier outcome labels, reported as accuracy-cost Pareto frontiers; the training recipe matches the project's.
what: Runs all three tiers offline on the training split, derives cost-aware oracle labels per cost parameter, trains lightweight classifiers to imitate them. Features are question, context and generator-output cues, available before verification. Frontiers beat fixed-tier policies across six generator models.
thesis_use: precedent for gain-labelled routing and Pareto reporting. Contrast: single answer, no candidate set, no uncertainty/random/oracle selector baselines (only fixed tiers).

title: Proof-of-Perception: Certified Tool-Using Multimodal Reasoning with Compositional Conformal Guarantees
relevance_note: HIGH — a controller that allocates tool calls under a budget from per-node conformal sets, stopping early otherwise
what: Multimodal reasoning is cast as an executable graph where each perception or logic node outputs a conformal set. A controller expands with extra tool calls only when the certificates say it is needed. Evaluated on document, chart and multi-image QA, where it improves over chain-of-thought, ReAct-style and program-of-thought baselines with more efficient compute (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: baseline variant (certificate-triggered scene-uncertainty selector) and a template for budget-aware calibrated stopping; not driving

title: Calibrate-Then-Delegate: Safety Monitoring with Risk and Budget Guarantees via Model Cascades
relevance_note: HIGH — a learned predictor of the benefit of an expensive call, calibrated to a budget or risk guarantee; direct analogue of expected-gain targets vs. uncertainty triggers
what: A cheap latent-space probe screens every input and hard cases are escalated to an expert. Existing cascades delegate on probe uncertainty; CTD instead trains a "delegation value" probe that predicts the benefit of replacing the probe score with the expert score, then calibrates a threshold on it with held-out data and multiple hypothesis testing for finite-sample guarantees on cost or safety performance. On four safety datasets it improves over uncertainty-based delegation over much of the budget range and avoids unnecessary expert calls.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (benefit-prediction target plus conformal threshold on it, for the calibration phase); supports the claim that uncertainty is a weak proxy for query value

title: To Call or Not to Call: A Framework to Assess and Optimize LLM Tool Calling
relevance_note: HIGH — decision-theoretic framing of whether to call a tool (necessity, utility, affordability) and a learned estimator that improves budgeted allocation
what: Evaluates six open models and one proprietary model across two tools and six tasks; perceived need and utility are misaligned with true values, especially under budget constraints, giving both overuse and harmful calls. Lightweight latent estimators of need (LNEs) trained on hidden states predict true need better than model self-reports and improve budgeted tool allocation.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (hidden-state need estimator, analogous to cached VLM embeddings feeding the selector); supports that prompting a model to choose tools is unreliable

title: Risk-Adaptive Edge--Cloud Visual Reasoning for Communication-Efficient Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — learns/decides when to call an expensive VLM under a cost (cloud request) budget in driving, trajectory-agnostic trigger.
what: Onboard VLM plus lightweight detector assess traffic and path-relative hazards and decide when to request cloud VLM advice. In CARLA it matched the task success of periodic cloud access with 54.1% fewer cloud requests and fewer AEB activations.
thesis_use: competitor/baseline family for the scene-uncertainty trigger; supports the accuracy-vs-query-cost framing.

title: Self-Aware Active Learning Enables Continual Improvement in Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — estimates when competence is insufficient and hands control to expert/fallback; evaluated incl. CARLA occlusion hazards.
what: A world model yields "fear" (short-horizon predictive risk and uncertainty) and "curiosity" (prediction error) signals; curiosity adapts the fear threshold for takeover. Evaluated on route transfer, Waymo logs, CARLA occlusion hazards and a mobile robot.
thesis_use: baseline for scene-level deferral; idea for adaptive threshold; fallback-policy phase.

title: Designing Versatile Samples for Learned Trajectory Scoring
relevance_note: HIGH — trained scorer that selects one trajectory from a candidate pool of a frozen planner.
what: Notes that planners' proposals cluster around safe modes, so supervision near decision boundaries is thin. Builds lateral/longitudinal perturbation generators of the logged trajectory as extra training samples; a transformer scorer on frozen DiffusionDrive and MeanFuser reaches 90.1 and 90.4 EPDMS on NAVSIM navtrain (gains of 0.4 and 0.3).
thesis_use: idea to borrow (candidate-set construction so candidates diverge near decision boundaries); ranker design.

title: When to Ask for Help: Uncertainty-Triggered Aerial Refinement for Off-Road Navigation
relevance_note: HIGH — planner-conditioned decision of whether and which measurement to request, by scoring the planner's own rollouts; closest conceptual match found in this slice.
what: UGV evaluates how uncertain map information affects its current MPPI rollouts. If navigation is degraded, it scores the same rollouts under resolved map hypotheses, selects the map layer with largest useful improvement, requests that aerial measurement, fuses it and replans. 180 simulation trials on three routes: 98.9% goal attainment, 87.7% less mean UAV flight time than continuous greedy aerial mapping; each second of UAV flight saves 2.94 s of UGV navigation time.
thesis_use: competitor-in-spirit and supporting evidence that candidate-conditioned acquisition beats uncertainty-only triggering; cite as related work (off-road, not driving).

title: Adaptive Submodularity: Theory and Applications in Active Learning and Stochastic Optimization
relevance_note: HIGH - adaptive greedy selection of observations with guarantees; sequential 'which observation next' under a budget.
what: Introduces adaptive submodularity; adaptive greedy is competitive with the optimal policy; examples include sensor placement and active learning.
thesis_use: Theory frame for a greedy expected-gain selector at budget 1 (our case is the single-step instance). Cite when justifying expected-gain targets.

title: Near-optimal Nonmyopic Value of Information in Graphical Models
relevance_note: HIGH - classic value-of-information subset selection with a (1-1/e) guarantee.
what: Gives a randomized algorithm with a constant-factor guarantee for selecting an observation subset in a graphical model, with a hardness result and experiments on two real datasets.
thesis_use: Classic VoI citation for 'select the observation with the highest expected value'. Our MLP regresses exactly such a per-tool expected gain.

title: Revisiting Active Perception
relevance_note: HIGH - the canonical active-perception reference; perception chosen for the task, not for fidelity.
what: Reviews the history of active perception ideas and argues the seminal contributions are as relevant today as decades ago given modern compute. Pair with Bajcsy's original 1988 Proc. IEEE paper (not fetched).
thesis_use: Cite for the framing 'perception acts as a function of the decision', the lineage behind our selector.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
relevance_note: HIGH - foundational risk-coverage selective prediction for deep nets.
what: Builds a selective classifier from a trained network that rejects instances to meet a user-set risk with high probability; 2% top-5 ImageNet error guaranteed at 99.9% with about 60% coverage.
thesis_use: Foundational citation for abstain and for risk-coverage curves; our Pareto is the cost analogue. Link to the conformal risk phase.

title: Learning to Maximize Mutual Information for Dynamic Feature Selection
relevance_note: HIGH - greedy conditional-mutual-information acquisition learned by amortization; the closest ML analogue of an expected-gain selector.
what: Selects features greedily by conditional mutual information; since that needs oracle access to the data distribution, learns it by amortized optimization; recovers the greedy policy at optimality and beats several feature selection methods.
thesis_use: Method to borrow or baseline: an information-gain selector with an abstain/stop option. Strong prior for the learned MLP selector.

title: A Language Agent for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH - earliest LLM driving agent with a tool library via function calls, before DriveAgent-R1.
what: Replaces the pipeline with an LLM that uses a tool library, a memory and a reasoning engine with chain-of-thought and self-reflection. The model calls tools for perception and prediction results; it does not decide a per-step budget.
thesis_use: Pre-DriveAgent-R1 tool-use citation. Contrast: tool calls are fixed, not selected under budget.

title: DriveAgent-R1: Advancing VLM-based Autonomous Driving with Active Perception and Hybrid Thinking
relevance_note: HIGH — the anchor/baseline. Facts verified from the v3 HTML: the final RL stage adds a tool-usage reward with a per-call cost C_tool = 0.25/2 = 0.125 (a 0.25 accuracy gain amortized over an expected median of 2 calls); tool-mode trajectories are rewarded relative to the mean of text-only trajectories. Output is high-level behavior (meta-actions), not a candidate set.
what: see the abstract (tools: RoI inspection, depth estimation, 3D detection; adaptive switch between text-only and tool reasoning on Drive-Internal and nuScenes).
thesis_use: baseline. Its trigger is scene complexity learned by RL and has no candidate-set input. A latency comparison of 7.91 s vs 6.74 s (always-tool vs adaptive) appeared only in a search summary: UNVERIFIED.

title: Safety Evaluation of Motion Plans Using Trajectory Predictors as Forward Reachable Set Estimators
relevance_note: HIGH for the future phase — a runtime safety monitor for an end-to-end plan using conformal-calibrated forward reachable sets plus a Bayesian OOD filter.
what: Complete (conformal coverage) and sound (Bayesian filter) monitor of ego-plan intersection with calibrated FRS of other agents; nuScenes (per search).
thesis_use: idea to borrow for conformal accept/reject; baseline for the calibrated monitor phase.

title: DriveCritic: Towards Context-Aware, Human-Aligned Evaluation for Autonomous Driving with Vision-Language Models
relevance_note: HIGH — a VLM trained (SFT then RL) to adjudicate between trajectory pairs using visual and symbolic context; a pairwise critic.
what: Dataset of challenging NAVSIM-style scenarios with pairwise human preferences, where EPDMS lacks context. Outperforms EPDMS and baselines at matching human preferences.
thesis_use: baseline for pairwise ranking; the pairwise formulation could replace the project's top-1 ranker in analysis.

title: Closed-Loop Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Language Driving Agents (DynaChain)
relevance_note: HIGH, learns which questions to ask per frame, value judged by the trajectory outcome
what: Formalises reasoning-chain selection as a closed-loop MDP; DynaChain decides at each frame which questions to ask before acting, trained with closed-loop agentic RL on Bench2Drive-VL. Raises Driving Score from 58.93 to 79.15 while asking 2.52 questions per decision instead of seven; the gain comes from which questions are asked, and requires learned selection plus closed-loop training. A fixed chain of questions drives worse than answering nothing.
thesis_use: competitor/related work; supports "selection matters more than answer accuracy". Contrast: question set is VLM reasoning, not perception tools, and it is not conditioned on candidate trajectories.

title: Learning When to Search: Adaptive Test-Time Computation for Generative Motion Planning
relevance_note: HIGH, decides whether to run candidate generation + scoring, trained from where search helps
what: Shows the benefit of candidate search varies across planning steps; a lightweight history-aware model decides after the base trajectory is generated whether to search. On nuPlan closed loop: score 86.07 with search on 56.81% of steps versus Full Search 85.64 at 100%; beats fixed schedules at similar rates.
thesis_use: related work for budget-vs-accuracy Pareto of a gate; it gates search over candidates, not perception tools; the gate sees the base trajectory (partly candidate-aware).

title: Foresight on Demand: Learning What and When to Predict for Autonomous Driving (FD-WAM)
relevance_note: HIGH, router trained on realised planning-score difference with vs without an extra information source
what: Utility-Aware Selective Foresight trains a router with the realised planning score difference between the planner's foresight and no-foresight paths, deciding from observed history alone; plus a decision-relevant foresight representation. Evaluated on NAVSIM v1/v2 and zero-shot HUGSIM. (Numbers not in abstract.)

title: HALP: Detecting Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models without Generating a Single Token
relevance_note: HIGH (method fit) — probes pre-generation hidden states of eight VLMs including Qwen2.5-VL-7B to predict an answer's failure, with abstention and selective routing named as uses. Three token families compared: visual-only features, vision tokens in the decoder, query-token states.

Abstract: "Late query-token states are the most predictive for most models" and the best layer and modality vary by architecture. title: Probing Visual Concepts in Lightweight Vision-Language Models for Automated Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — linear probes on activations of five VLMs for driving concepts; separates perceptual failure (not linearly encoded) from cognitive failure (encoded but answered wrong); object distance degrades linear separability quickly.

thesis_use: motivates why prompting says "none" (cognitive failure) and why a distance tool is needed (distance concept degrades); template for probing Qwen3.5-9B per layer on the project's hazard types.

title: LLM Agents Already Know When to Call Tools -- Even Without Reasoning
venue: arXiv preprint (NeurIPS 2026 poster page seen in search, not on arXiv abs)
relevance_note: HIGH — direct evidence that a linear probe beats prompted/verbalized tool decisions.
what: Benchmark of 18 environments with controlled tool-necessity boundaries. Prompt-only baselines suppress necessary calls along with unnecessary ones; Reason-then-Act costs accuracy on hard tasks. Tool necessity is linearly decodable from pre-generation hidden states with AUROC 0.89-0.96 across six models; Probe&Prefill reduces tool calls by 38% with 1.7% accuracy loss (abstract and Sec. 1; a 48% figure in a search snippet was wrong; Sec. 1 also reports up to 56% fewer API calls on Search-o1 without accuracy loss).

title: Lost in Fog: Sensor Perturbations Expose Reasoning Fragility in Driving VLAs
relevance_note: HIGH — known anchor; id now resolved.
what: Alpamayo R1 (10B) over 1,996 scenarios and 8 perturbations (noise at 4 levels, 2 lighting extremes, 2 fog levels). When the Chain-of-Causation explanation changes, trajectory deviation rises 5.3x (21.8 m vs 4.1 m). Evaluation is open-loop.
thesis_use: motivation for tool-noise levels; reasoning-consistency as a possible trigger signal.

title: BOKBO (Best of K Bad Options): Calibrated Abstention for VLA Policies
relevance_note: HIGH (method fit) — conformal abstention over K candidate actions when all may be unsafe; K-candidate structure like the project's.

Finds policy-internal nonconformity scores correlate 0.98 with sampling noise and at noise floor with violations; a learned violation predictor on semantic visual features supports calibration (libero_object_temp_x0.1, OpenVLA-OFT, eps=0.05: conditional bound holds on 86% of bootstrap splits, 78% coverage, 70% net success). Manipulation, not driving.
thesis_use: idea to borrow for the abstain/fallback layer; cautions that candidate-disagreement scores can be uninformative.

title: BLUE: Toward Better Language Use in Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — a gate on frozen VLA hidden states decides per frame whether the costly step (language) is worth running.
what: Shows language helps or hurts on a small fraction of routes; scene complexity and kinematics alone struggle to predict benefit, but pretrained hidden states encode it. 0.11M-parameter gate gives 76.2% success on Bench2Drive, 36 DS on Longest6 v2, 2.54x speedup, +8.9% success over backbone.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (train the selector on LLM hidden states, not only image embeddings; benefit labels derived without extra annotation, similar to expected-gain targets). Supports the claim that geometry-only scene features are insufficient for the trigger.

title: DriveJudge: Rethinking Autonomous Driving Evaluation with Vision-Language Models
relevance_note: HIGH — an evaluation agent that interprets context with a VLM and then selectively invokes deterministic rule functions. This is "VLM that calls tools" applied to judging trajectories.
what: 33,577 human-annotated samples; tasks Driving Quality Classification and Trajectory Preference Selection. Beats EPDMS by 21.23 AUC on classification and DriveCritic by 6.5% on preference selection (abstract).
thesis_use: closest tool-calling-over-trajectories design; competitor in spirit (tools called after the VLM reads context, but no budget analysis).

title: Look Again Before You Abstain:Budgeted Conformal Evidence Acquisition for Reliable Vision-Language Model
relevance_note: HIGH — three-way answer/abstain/acquire-more-visual-evidence (zoom, crop) with conformal risk control under a bounded budget.
what: A conformal claim filter must abstain on over 80% of claims to hold hallucination below 5% on a balanced object-existence benchmark; BCEA lets the model instead re-examine the image under a bounded budget. The abstract I could retrieve cut off before the headline result.
thesis_use: template for the future accept/inspect/fallback phase; competitor for the "calibrated query" story.

title: Calibration Is Not Control: Intervention Value for LLM-Agent Oversight
relevance_note: HIGH (conceptual) — argues intervention triggered by calibrated failure risk is the wrong target; train on intervention utility.
what: On ALFWorld, changing the supervision target from failure to intervention utility lowers regret from 0.51 to 0.09 with features/estimator/router fixed; online on 300 unseen tasks a frozen prefix-feature controller hands off less often (35% vs 48%) and succeeds more (45% vs 37%). Gains small on two reasoning benchmarks.
thesis_use: supports expected-gain targets over scene-uncertainty triggering; cite for the contrast between risk and value.

title: DriveVer: Lightweight Trajectory Evaluator as Test-Time Verifier for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — a plug-and-play verifier that takes candidate trajectories, multi-view features and ego kinematics and outputs a safety confidence and a refinement vector; maps to the accept/replan phase and to the ranker.
what: Dual-head 34M-parameter verifier trained on a NAVSIM trajectory set (16 trajectories per scene with scores from low to high). Improves base planners on NAVSIM v1/v2, e.g. DiffusionDrive +0.9 PDMS; ELF-VLA 91.0 to 91.5 (html table).
thesis_use: baseline for learned ranker/verifier; shows gains are around +0.5 to +0.9, comparable in size to the project's VLM-embedding gain.

title: The Illusion of Visual Tool-Use: A Causal Audit of Thinking with Images
venue: EMNLP 2026 Findings (venue from a search listing only; not on the arXiv abs page)
relevance_note: HIGH — evidence that VLM visual-tool policies are mis-called, plus a step-level "Visual Evidence Gain" estimand (counterfactual replacement of one observation).
what: Audits six models on five fine-grained perception benchmarks at policy, trajectory, and step level. Finds "Calling Without Looking" (observations have no causal effect) and "Looking Without Planning" (informative observations, incoherent call schedule); accuracy gain concentrated in a calibrated minority.
thesis_use: motivates learned selection; Visual Evidence Gain is a per-observation counterfactual gain similar in spirit to your expected-gain target.

title: Barrier Function Conformal Safety Clearance Certification with CVaR for Driving Trajectory Selection
relevance_note: HIGH — conformal certificate on the *selected* trajectory among planner candidates (post-selection calibration).
what: Differentiable separating-axis barrier margin lower-bounds oriented-box clearance; plan-time margin (nominal or sampled lower-tail CVaR) is calibrated post selection over exchangeable drive sessions. On 300 frozen nuPlan sessions with PDM closed-loop proposals at 10% miscoverage, CVaR cuts the conformal correction from 1.43 m to 0.03 m and raises nonnegative-clearance certificates from 68.7% to 87.3%; coverage 93.3-96.7%.
thesis_use: idea to borrow for accept gate after ranker; note post-selection calibration issue.

title: Observe Before You Alert: Adaptive Driver Alerting with Vision-Language Models
relevance_note: HIGH — frozen-ish Qwen3-VL-4B hidden states, pooled from structured spans, feed a tri-action policy SILENT/OBSERVE/ALERT; OBSERVE delays and gathers evidence.
what: Pools hidden states from structured belief spans for danger estimation and policy prediction; VLAlert-Bench from four dashcam datasets. AUROC 0.689 vs 0.610 baseline, AP_tick 0.195 vs 0.176, DAUS 0.4878 vs 0.4752 (abstract). The linear probe AUROC 0.894 is confirmed in the full text (Table 3a).
thesis_use: idea to borrow for the future accept/inspect/replan phase (an OBSERVE action) and for reading hidden states at structured token positions. Full text (see addendum) confirms the backbone is LoRA-adapted in stage 1 and then frozen for all heads.

title: Driving on Registers, Reasoning on Risk: Risk-Aware Occupancy for Register-Based End-to-End Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — measures an oracle-best-of-K gap directly and uses "candidate-conditioned risk queries" for selection.
what: Abstract: "On a register-based baseline, bad and poor candidates constitute 19.74% of the candidate set, while the oracle-best candidate ranks only 33.9th on average." Candidate-conditioned risk queries on a risk-aware occupancy representation lift selected-trajectory PDMS to 0.951 vs 0.937 baseline (+1.5% relative), average candidate PDMS by 7.7%, and Spearman correlation among good candidates from 0.26 to 0.67. They first use an oracle RiskOcc (their dataset RiskOcc4D-NAVSIM) and then "move beyond this oracle setting" with an external RiskOcc predictor from sensors, described as competitive.
thesis_use: direct evidence for the fair-ceiling framing (oracle vs predicted perception, as the project does with privileged state vs noisy tools); competitor-in-spirit for "candidate-conditioned queries", though it queries a learned occupancy field rather than choosing among tools under a budget.

title: DriveReferee: Geometric Safety Verdicts Need Not Be Learned for Driving World-Action Models
relevance_note: HIGH — an analytic geometric collision/drivable-area check on a predicted scene state, used to verify candidate trajectories and select a safer one; mirrors the project's collision-check tool and the later accept/replan phase.
what: A learned geometry readout predicts the scene representation from camera input, then an explicit rule evaluates collision and drivable area for each candidate. Under matched candidates and budgets it matches or beats learned-verifier and heuristic baselines, and learning the verdict gives no measurable downstream gain. 92.02 PDMS on NAVSIM navtest with single-camera input.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (deterministic collision check as the verifier; supports treating the tool as rule-based and noisy only through the state estimate); baseline-style comparison for learned vs analytic verification.

title: Evaluation Is All You Need for Multi-Modal Autonomous Driving
venue: ICLR 2027 desk rejected submission; arXiv preprint
relevance_note: HIGH for the ranker side, names the generation-evaluation asymmetry: oracle best candidate is strong but planners fail to select it
what: Unified trajectory evaluator (Safety-aware Scorer plus VLM-guided Modulator weighting criteria per scene) and an oracle-aligned objective. Desk rejected, so treat as a preprint-level claim.
thesis_use: motivates oracle-best-candidate scoring; ranker/critic baseline idea.

title: Localized Conformal Safety Monitoring with Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: HIGH — frozen VLM plus split-conformal layer that labels planned trajectories safe/unsafe with finite-sample coverage; template for the calibration phase.
what: SLLCP, label-conditional split conformal with localization that upweights relevant past scenes when computing thresholds. On 15k CARLA trajectories from unseen scenarios it flags 89.6% (Qwen) and 88.4% (Cosmos) of collision-causing trajectories, vs 4.6% and 39.1% for the base VLMs.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (localized, label-conditional calibration for accept/veto); baseline for future-phase monitor.

title: DiVeR: Decision-Critical Verifier Learning for VLA Test-Time Scaling
relevance_note: HIGH (idea) — measures from the dispersion of sampled action candidates how decision-critical a state is. This is a candidate-divergence signal, the same family as the project's candidate-conditioned features, but in manipulation and used for verifier training.
what: Verifier-guided test-time scaling samples multiple action candidates and picks the most likely to succeed. DiVeR estimates decision criticality from dispersion of sampled action representations and reweights verifier learning toward states where choice matters, with no step-level labels. Improves success on LIBERO, RoboCasa and a Franka robot.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (candidate dispersion as a feature or as justification for candidate-conditioned triggering); contrast: it reweights training, it does not choose a perception query.

title: Not All Uncertainty Matters: Simulation-in-the-Loop Fast-Slow Reasoning for Decision-Critical Autonomous Driving System
relevance_note: HIGH — planner-conditioned decision on whether to request extra information (expected planning gain), measured against periodic/uncertainty triggers; closest overlap to the project's selector idea.
what: Fast-slow collaboration where an onboard planner is embedded in uncertainty assessment; it simulates plausible scene realizations, estimates the expected reduction in planning cost if uncertainty is resolved (EPG), and uses EPG for cloud invocation, guidance integration and request prioritization under deadlines. In CARLA, vs fixed-period collaboration: 50% fewer unnecessary cloud interactions, over 6% higher navigation success, up to 26.2% shorter finish time (dynamic scenarios).
thesis_use: competitor / related work for "value-of-information style, plan-conditioned querying"; borrow EPG as a name/metric for expected-gain targets. Differs: cloud VLM guidance, not perception-tool choice, no candidate-set divergence.

title: Slow Brain, Fast Planner: Latency-Resilient VLM-Augmented Urban Navigation
relevance_note: MED-HIGH — VLM selects an index from a planner's candidate-trajectory set (the "trajectory scoring gap"); same first author as Counterfactual VLA.
what: Defines a "trajectory scoring gap" between the planner's top choice and the best candidate. VLM selection gives 30% ADE reduction on about 2,000 real scenarios; a fusion layer turns a stale 1-3 s VLM choice into real-time scoring via geometric similarity with exponential decay. Score fusion keeps >80% success with delays up to 5 s (abstract).
thesis_use: related work for the candidate-set ranker side; no perception tools, so not an overlap on the selector.

title: Active Information Gathering for Long-Horizon Navigation Under Uncertainty by Learning the Value of Information
relevance_note: MED (classic) — learned VoI of revealing unseen space, GNN trained on tractable training-time VoI; up to 63.76% and 36.68% cost improvements over non-learned and learned baselines.

title: Learnable Conformal Prediction with Context-Aware Nonconformity Functions for Robotic Planning and Perception
relevance_note: MED — context-aware conformal sets for detection (BDD100K, Cityscapes) and path planning; relevant to calibrating planner accept/reject.
what: LCP replaces fixed nonconformity scores with a lightweight neural function using geometric, semantic and task features. Reduces classification set sizes by 18%, gives 46-54% tighter boxes on COCO, BDD100K and Cityscapes, and raises path-planning success from 72% to 91.5% with 4.5% path inflation vs. 12.2% for standard CP.
thesis_use: Idea to borrow: learned nonconformity scores using geometric features, for the calibration phase.

title: Safe Planning in Unknown Environments Using Conformalized Semantic Maps
relevance_note: MED (borderline) — conformal uncertainty on perception feeding a planner with a user-specified mission completion rate.
what: Quantifies uncertainty in on-the-fly semantic maps with conformal prediction, model- and distribution-free, and plans paths achieving user-specified completion rates without sensor-model knowledge.
thesis_use: Related work for conformal perception-to-planner guarantees.

title: CPATTA: Conformal Supervision Allocation For Active Test-Time Adaptation
relevance_note: MED — allocates a limited annotation-query budget using conformal scores; shows that conformal selection beats heuristic uncertainty triggering.
what: Brings conformal uncertainty with coverage-aware online calibration into active test-time adaptation, with a domain-shift detector and staged updates. Outperforms state-of-the-art ATTA methods by around 5% accuracy.
thesis_use: Supporting evidence that principled scores beat heuristic scene-uncertainty at equal query budget (different domain).

title: AIM-CoT: Active Information-driven Multimodal Chain-of-Thought for Vision-Language Reasoning
relevance_note: MED — addresses 'what to see' (evidence selection) and 'when to see' (triggering) with information-driven rather than attention-based signals.
what: Argues interleaved-modal CoT depends on selecting visual evidence and on when to insert it, and that attention signals and existing triggers fall short; proposes an active information-driven framework (abstract truncated before results).
thesis_use: Related work for evidence selection and triggering in VLMs.

title: NuRisk: A Visual Question Answering Dataset for Agent-Level Risk Assessment in Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — agent-level risk VQA on BEV sequences; 2.9K scenarios, 1.1M agent-level samples.
what: Benchmarked VLMs peak at 33% accuracy at high latency; a fine-tuned 7B VLM agent reaches 41% with 75% lower latency.
thesis_use: evidence that frozen VLMs reason poorly about risk, matching the project's finding that the VLM mostly says "none".

title: INSIGHT: INference-time Sequence Introspection for Generating Help Triggers in Vision-Language-Action Models
relevance_note: MED — learns when to request help (an abstain/defer decision) but from the policy's own token uncertainty, manipulation setting.
what: Extracts per-token entropy, log-probability and Dirichlet-based aleatoric/epistemic estimates from pi0-FAST and trains compact transformers to predict help triggers, under strong and weak supervision, in-distribution and OOD. Finds that modeling the temporal evolution of uncertainty beats static sequence-level scores.
thesis_use: baseline-style "uncertainty trigger" comparison; idea for the later abstain/fallback phase.

title: Calibrating the Full Predictive Class Distribution of 3D Object Detectors for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — confidence calibration of detector class outputs; relevant to noisy-tool confidences and the future calibration phase.
what: Auxiliary calibration losses plus isotonic regression give best calibration for CenterPoint and PillarNet; DSVT-Pillar cannot be jointly calibrated.
thesis_use: background for the calibration phase.

title: More Than Meets the Eye? Uncovering the Reasoning-Planning Disconnect in Training Vision-Language Driving Models
relevance_note: MED — shows driving VLM planning depends on ego/navigation priors rather than chain-of-thought; consistent with the project's finding that prompting the VLM to pick tools is weak.
what: Builds DriveMind (plan-aligned CoT VQA from nuPlan), trains VLM agents with SFT and GRPO; removing priors causes large drops while removing CoT changes little. Proposes a training-free perturbation probe of prior reliance.
thesis_use: supports "contradicts the assumption that VLM reasoning drives decisions"; motivation for a learned geometry-feature selector.

title: Verifier-free Test-Time Sampling for Vision-Language-Action Models
relevance_note: MED — selects among multiple candidate actions with an internal confidence metric, no external verifier.
what: MG-Select uses KL divergence from a reference action-token distribution (the same VLA with randomly masked state and language) as confidence for choosing among candidates, with joint training via dropout of conditions. Reports consistent improvements across simulation and real-world benchmarks (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: cheap verifier-free selection baseline idea.

title: Precise and Efficient Collision Prediction under Uncertainty in Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — two semi-analytic collision probabilities for planned trajectories under pose/velocity uncertainty; a principled version of the geometric collision-check tool.
what: Matches Monte Carlo results with large runtime savings (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: idea to borrow for the collision-check tool under noise.

title: Scalable Offline Metrics for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — offline metrics correlate poorly with closed-loop outcomes; an epistemic-uncertainty offline metric improves correlation by over 13%.
what: Simulation analysis plus real-world validation.
thesis_use: caveat for the open-loop evaluation; cite as limitation.

title: Learning-To-Measure: In-Context Active Feature Acquisition
relevance_note: MED — acquisition policy via uncertainty-guided greedy conditional mutual information, with in-context generalization across tasks.
what: Formalizes meta-AFA and proposes L2M: autoregressive pre-training for uncertainty quantification under arbitrary missingness plus a greedy CMI acquisition agent, operating in-context without per-task retraining. Matches or surpasses task-specific baselines on tabular benchmarks, especially with scarce labels and high missingness.
thesis_use: Related work only; tabular domain.

title: Safe Driving in Occluded Environments
relevance_note: MED — probabilistic safety certificate for latent risk from occluded objects, usable in MPC or learned policies; tested in CARLA.
what: Probabilistic invariance gives linear action constraints that bound the latent risk probability, without needing the hidden objects observed.
thesis_use: related work for occlusion hazards and for the accept/fallback phase.

title: Perfect Prediction or Plenty of Proposals? What Matters Most in Planning for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — on Val14 and interPlan, perfect prediction does not improve planning; proposal quality matters, with predictions used mainly for collision checks.
what: A PDM-based planner with better diverse proposals outperforms existing methods.
thesis_use: supports the candidate-set emphasis; a proposal generator for candidates.

title: Do What You Say: Steering Vision-Language-Action Models via Runtime Reasoning-Action Alignment Verification
relevance_note: MED — samples multiple candidate action sequences, predicts outcomes by simulation, and has a VLM pick the best; a candidate-set selector with a VLM.
what: Training-free runtime steering for reasoning VLAs: sample candidates from the same model, predict outcomes via simulation, a pre-trained VLM selects the one aligned with the textual plan. Reports up to 15% gain over prior work on behavior composition tasks (LIBERO-100 extension).
thesis_use: idea to borrow for the ranker; evidence for VLM-as-selector design.

title: Conformal Prediction in The Loop: A Feedback-Based Uncertainty Model for Trajectory Optimization
relevance_note: MED — conformal prediction regions fed back from realized trajectories into planning with a joint risk constraint; relevant to the calibrated-risk future phase.
what: Feedback-Based CP (Fb-CP) for shrinking-horizon trajectory optimization, with CP-based posterior risk calculation, decision-focused iterative risk allocation, and an extension to distribution shift. Coverage guarantees proven; benchmark results not quantified in the abstract.
thesis_use: idea for conformal risk control in the accept/replan policy.

title: Reliable Inference in Edge-Cloud Model Cascades via Conformal Alignment
relevance_note: MED — calibrated escalation from a cheap to an expensive model with a tunable coverage/deferral-rate trade-off.
what: Casts escalation from edge to cloud as multiple hypothesis testing, using conformal alignment to select inputs that can safely be handled at the edge, with guarantees on the fraction of edge decisions meeting cloud-level conditional coverage. Exposes a trade-off among coverage, deferral rate and set size.
thesis_use: Idea to borrow: calibrated 'call the expensive tool or not' guarantee.

title: Occluded nuScenes: A Multi-Sensor Dataset for Evaluating Perception Robustness in Automated Driving
relevance_note: MED — parameterised, reproducible occlusions for camera (four types), radar and LiDAR (three degradations each).
what: Extension of nuScenes for controlled sensor degradation; supports robustness evaluation of fusion models.
thesis_use: benchmark reference for occlusion injection design; not a decision benchmark.

title: Energy-Efficient Autonomous Driving with Adaptive Perception and Robust Decision
relevance_note: MED — compute-budgeted perception: selects perception model and framerate by a scene-difficulty classifier, plus an RL decision module robust to perturbed perception.
what: EneAD tunes perception "knobs" with Bayesian optimisation and switches them per scenario; it reports perception consumption reduced by 1.9x to 3.5x (rest of the abstract is cut off in my fetch).
thesis_use: cost-axis related work; scene-difficulty switching is another trajectory-agnostic trigger.

title: Alpamayo-R1: Bridging Reasoning and Action Prediction for Generalizable Autonomous Driving in the Long Tail
relevance_note: MED — reasoning VLA with a diffusion trajectory decoder; up to 12% planning-accuracy gain on challenging cases and 35% fewer close encounters in closed-loop simulation.
what: Chain of Causation dataset, Cosmos-Reason backbone, SFT then RL; RL improves reasoning quality by 45% and reasoning-action consistency by 37%.
thesis_use: VLM/VLA driving anchor; no tool use.

title: Who Moved My Distribution? Conformal Prediction for Interactive Multi-Agent Systems
relevance_note: MED — conformal prediction regions for other agents' trajectories used by the ego controller; names the endogenous distribution shift that closed-loop evaluation would face.
what: Iterative conformal framework adapting an uncertainty-aware ego controller to the endogenous shift caused by reactive agents, with convergence conditions; in 2- and 3-agent simulations it improves success rates by up to 9.6% over CP baselines.
thesis_use: Caveat for moving from open-loop to closed-loop calibration.

title: LAVQA: A Latency-Aware Visual Question Answering Framework for Shared Autonomy in Self-Driving Vehicles
relevance_note: MED — when uncertainty is high the vehicle halts and asks a remote human via VQA; a defer/ask-for-help setting with a latency-aware risk map.
what: Adds a Latency-Induced Collision Map to visual queries. Closed-loop CARLA simulation: collision rates reduced by over 8x against latency-agnostic baselines.
thesis_use: related work for the future inspect/fallback phase.

title: VLA-R: Vision-Language Action Retrieval toward Open-World End-to-End Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — uses a frozen VLM for open-world detection/segmentation features feeding an action retrieval head; frozen-VLM-features-to-planner pattern.
what: Frozen VLM perception features, a Q-Former bottleneck, and vision-action contrastive learning for action retrieval; real-world robotic platform demos, no numbers in abstract.
thesis_use: related work for the frozen-VLM-embedding input to the selector.

title: Enhancing LLM-based Autonomous Driving with Modular Traffic Light and Sign Recognition
relevance_note: MED — a dedicated traffic-light/sign recogniser feeds an LLM driver, i.e. a perception tool for small safety-critical objects; always-on rather than selected.
what: TLS-Assist turns detections into structured text for the LLM input; closed loop on LangAuto in CARLA, up to 14% relative improvement over LMDrive and 7% over BEVDriver.
thesis_use: evidence that a light-state tool helps; an always-on baseline point for the Pareto curve.

title: When to Think and When to Look: Uncertainty-Guided Lookback
relevance_note: MED — uncertainty-triggered look-back to the image in VLM reasoning; an uncertainty-triggered 'look' baseline in the style of scene-uncertainty triggering.
what: Evaluates ten InternVL3.5 and Qwen3-VL variants on MMMU-val, shows more thinking is not always better, and proposes a training-free decoding strategy combining an uncertainty signal with adaptive lookback prompts and breadth search, improving MMMU under fixed token budgets.
thesis_use: Baseline-style trigger; not driving.

title: Time-aware Motion Planning in Dynamic Environments with Conformal Prediction
relevance_note: MED — conformal prediction in a planner with an adaptive quantile that tightens margins where uncertainty is high.
what: Global planner (SIPP) with distribution-free safety guarantees and a local reactive planner using adaptive CP; the quantile is tuned automatically rather than fixed. Numerical experiments in dynamic cluttered environments; no numbers in abstract.
thesis_use: idea for adaptive conformal thresholds in the accept/inspect decision.

title: DeeAD: Dynamic Early Exit of Vision-Language Action for Efficient Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — driving VLA that decides when to stop computing by checking intermediate trajectories against planning priors; a when-to-compute decision tied to trajectories.
what: Training-free early exit that terminates when predicted trajectories agree with lightweight planning priors within a deviation under 2 m, with a multi-hop layer-skipping controller. On Bench2Drive with ORION: up to 28% transformer-layer sparsity and 29% latency reduction while preserving planning quality and safety.
thesis_use: related work on trajectory-conditioned compute gating; shows the cost-vs-quality framing in driving.

title: WaymoQA: A Multi-View Visual Question Answering Dataset for Safety-Critical Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — 35,000 human-annotated QA pairs for safety-critical reasoning where avoiding one risk can create another; MLLMs underperform on these versus normal scenes.
what: Two-stage task (resolve immediate risk, then downstream risk); fine-tuning on the dataset improves reasoning.
thesis_use: benchmark / VLM-weakness evidence.

title: Seeing before Observable: Potential Risk Reasoning in Autonomous Driving via Vision Language Models
relevance_note: MED — risks not yet observable, inferred from precursors; dataset PotentialRiskQA and a VLM framework PR-Reasoner.
what: Fine-tuning on PotentialRiskQA improves potential-risk reasoning over baseline VLMs (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: hazard-type taxonomy for occlusion scenarios; VLM baseline.

title: Sample-Efficient Expert Query Control in Active Imitation Learning via Conformal Prediction
relevance_note: MED — a calibrated rule for when to query an expert, with alpha tied to the expected query rate; matches the 'when to query' and calibration themes, but state-novelty based (trajectory-agnostic).
what: CRSAIL queries the expert only when the visited state is under-represented in the expert dataset; novelty is the distance to the K-th nearest expert state and a global threshold is set by a conformal quantile. On MuJoCo tasks it matches or exceeds expert-level reward while cutting expert queries by up to 96% vs. DAgger and up to 65% vs. prior active IL methods.
thesis_use: Idea to borrow: conformal threshold giving direct control of query rate for the future calibration phase; example of a scene-uncertainty-style trigger baseline.

title: LEC: Linear Expectation Constraints for Selection-Conditioned Risk Control in Selective Prediction and Routing Systems
relevance_note: MED — finite-sample selection-conditioned error control for accept/defer decisions, extended to routing to a second model; relevant to the calibrated accept/reject phase.
what: Controls the ratio of expected accepted errors to expected accepted predictions, giving a risk-constrained, retention-maximizing threshold from a held-out calibration set. Extends to two-model routing where the input is delegated if primary uncertainty exceeds its threshold; evaluated on QA and VQA.
thesis_use: Idea to borrow: accept-threshold calibration with error guarantee conditioned on acceptance, for the accept/inspect/replan/fallback policy.

title: Real-World Reinforcement Learning of Active Perception Behaviors
relevance_note: MED — trains active perception policies using privileged sensors only at training time, analogous to oracle labels from privileged simulator state.
what: AAWR (asymmetric advantage weighted regression) uses privileged extra sensors during training to learn high-quality value functions that estimate the advantage of the target policy, bootstrapping from few suboptimal demonstrations and a coarse policy.
thesis_use: Idea to borrow: privileged-information value targets for learning the selector.

title: Situation-Aware Interactive MPC Switching for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — learned classifier decides when to invoke the expensive controller, a compute-vs-accuracy gating of the same shape as tool calling.
what: Compares MPC formulations of different interaction fidelity, ranks them, and trains a neural classifier to switch among them. Invokes the advanced MPC only in rare critical situations; the abstract claims better overall performance with significantly lower compute (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: related work for "when to call the costly module"; scene-triggered baseline analogue.

title: Learning When to Look: A Disentangled Curriculum for Strategic Perception in Multimodal Reasoning
relevance_note: MED — RL policy for when to perceive, with a reward coupling perceptual actions to uncertainty markers.
what: Separates 'how-to-think' from 'when-to-look' with a text-only SFT curriculum then Perception-Grounded CoT, and trains timing by RL with a Pivotal Perception Reward linking looks to markers of cognitive uncertainty.
thesis_use: Related work for 'when to look' policies; trigger is language-uncertainty, not candidate-conditioned.

title: KnowVal: A Knowledge-Augmented and Value-Guided Autonomous Driving System
relevance_note: MED — Value Model trained on human preferences for trajectory assessment, plus LLM knowledge retrieval (a retrieval "query" step).
what: Builds a driving knowledge graph (laws, defensive driving, ethics) with LLM retrieval and trains a Value Model to guide value-aligned trajectory assessment. Lowest collision rate on nuScenes; state-of-the-art on Bench2Drive and NVISIM (per abstract).
thesis_use: trajectory critic related work.

title: LSRE: Latent Semantic Rule Encoding for Real-Time Semantic Risk Detection in Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — avoids per-frame VLM queries by distilling sparse VLM judgments into a latent classifier; VLM-cost and frozen-VLM-signal angle, CARLA.
what: Converts sparsely sampled VLM judgments into decision boundaries in a recurrent world model's latent space, enabling 10 Hz semantic risk assessment. On six CARLA semantic-failure scenarios it reaches accuracy comparable to a large VLM baseline with earlier hazard anticipation.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (distill VLM into cheap head); related work for VLM-in-the-loop cost.

title: RISE: Adaptive Imagination for World Action Models
relevance_note: MED — sequential Roll/Stop decision on the expected planning benefit of more computation, trained with counterfactual supervision. Driving (NAVSIM, nuScenes). Whether, not which.
what: A Latent Evaluator estimates risk and the possible planning improvement, a Rollout Gate trades benefit against compute. Introduces CounterDrive, a counterfactual dataset with expert annotation. Reports best overall planning with less unnecessary rollout (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: related work for expected-benefit gating; counterfactual data construction idea.

title: Imagine then Verify: Affordance-Targeted Active Perception for Task-Oriented Grasping in Cluttered Scenes (ATAP)
relevance_note: MED — viewpoint planner that maximises expected entropy reduction over competing occlusion hypotheses plus expected verification gain; stops on a viewpoint budget.
what: Hypothesises hidden geometry with a shape prior, predicts an affordance distribution, scores views. 57% fewer NBV steps than reconstruction-based active perception. Not learned from gain targets.
thesis_use: robot-manipulation analogue of (a)+(b) for occlusion; analytic rule, no selector baselines.

title: An Adaptive Multimodal End-to-End Autonomous Driving Framework Based on Behavior Discrepancy (G-VLM)
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems 27(10), pp. 13113 to 13124
relevance_note: MED — a learned gate trained from the discrepancy between a lightweight controller and the VLM-assisted output (a gain-style label), decides when to run the expensive semantic module. Binary, no candidate set.
what: G-VLM gates the expensive VLM on scene context and confidence estimates. CARLA closed-loop: 96.8% of the always-invoked VLM driving score at 12.2% of its compute, and up to 9.8 driving-score points over compute-matched alternatives (abstract).
thesis_use: baseline family for "when to call" gates with gain labels; supports the argument that "which tool" is the unaddressed part.
first_author: not captured from the page (Beijing Institute of Technology repository record)

title: Drive-P2D: A Progressive Perception-to-Decision Benchmark for VLMs in Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — benchmark that separates perception from decision for driving VLMs and covers high-risk scenarios; useful for justifying where VLMs fail.
what: 6,650 questions across Object, Scene and Decision levels with objective scoring of final answers and analysis of reasoning errors; evaluates mainstream VLMs on all and high-risk scenarios.
thesis_use: related work / motivation for tool-assisted perception.

title: Learning Contextual Runtime Monitors for Safe AI-Based Autonomy
relevance_note: MED — a context-conditioned monitor that selects among controllers, learned with contextual bandits, with safety guarantees, validated in two simulated driving scenarios.
what: Reformulates safe control ensembles as contextual monitoring: a monitor observes the context and selects the controller best suited to it, using contextual multi-armed bandit techniques. Reports significant safety and performance gains over non-contextual baselines in two simulated driving scenarios.
thesis_use: Related work for learned selectors in driving; bandit framing is an alternative to the MLP selector on expected-gain targets.

title: CoFreeVLA: Short-Horizon Collision-Free Dual-Arm Manipulation via Vision-Language-Action Model and Risk Estimation
relevance_note: MED — a calibrated risk estimator over candidate action sequences gates risky commands; structure similar to accept/reject of plans.
what: Lightweight short-horizon self-collision risk estimator taking proprioception, visual embeddings and candidate action sequences; gates commands and synthesizes recovery. Across five bimanual tasks and six VLA backbones, collision rate falls from 0.54 to 0.23 and success rises from 0.45 to 0.61.
thesis_use: idea for the gate/fallback phase (manipulation, so only the pattern transfers).

title: MTDrive: Multi-turn Interactive Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — MLLM iteratively refines trajectories from environmental feedback; multi-turn loop analogous to a look-then-decide agent (feedback is not a perception tool though).
what: mtGRPO computes relative advantages across turns; interactive trajectory-understanding dataset from closed-loop simulation; NAVSIM results claimed superior; 2.5x training throughput from system optimizations.
thesis_use: competitor-adjacent related work for multi-turn driving agents.

title: Conformal Thinking: Risk Control for Reasoning on a Compute Budget
relevance_note: MED — turns budget setting into distribution-free risk control with an upper stop threshold and a lower threshold; a template for choosing the query-budget operating point.
what: Reframes the token-budget problem as limiting error rate while minimizing compute, with an upper threshold (stop when confident) and a parametric lower threshold (stop unsolvable instances), set by distribution-free risk control from a validation set. Shows compute efficiency gains while meeting the user target risk across reasoning tasks.
thesis_use: Idea to borrow: choose the budget/threshold on the Pareto curve by risk control rather than by hand (future phase).

title: A Unified Candidate Set with Scene-Adaptive Refinement via Diffusion for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — multi-candidate generate-and-select with a shared scorer; candidate-set design matters for how candidates diverge.
what: Keeps fixed-vocabulary candidates and adds vocabulary-conditioned diffusion candidates, jointly scored by one selection module; HATNA smooths diffusion candidates. Evaluated on NAVSIM v1 and v2 (abstract gives no numbers).
thesis_use: source of candidate sets/scorers for later real-data phase.

title: VGAS: Value-Guided Action-Chunk Selection for Few-Shot Vision-Language-Action Adaptation
relevance_note: MED — best-of-N critic that must rank near-miss candidates; relevant to ranking quality when candidates are close.
what: Generation-selection framework: a fine-tuned VLA proposes, a geometric Transformer critic (Q-Chunk-Former) with Explicit Geometric Regularization selects, keeping action-ranking resolution among near-miss candidates. Claims consistent success and robustness gains; no numbers in the abstract.
thesis_use: idea for the ranker/critic; related work on near-tie candidates.

title: Scaling Verification Can Be More Effective than Scaling Policy Learning for Vision-Language-Action Alignment
relevance_note: MED — test-time verification over generated candidates; accuracy-versus-compute scaling framing similar to the Pareto view.
what: CoVer, a contrastive verifier, with CoVer-VLA: generate candidates over rephrased instructions, then select with the verifier. Reports 22% in-distribution and 13% OOD gains on SIMPLER, 45% in real-world, and on PolaRiS 14% task progress and 9% success rate.
thesis_use: related work on test-time selection; scaling-vs-budget argument.

title: Selective Perception for Robot: Task-Aware Attention in Multimodal VLA
relevance_note: MED — lightweight router decides which camera views to feed the policy based on predicted task relevance, with compute proportional to relevance; a budgeted input-selection decision (manipulation).
what: Adaptive routing on the text prompt and wrist camera predicts view relevance, attenuating low-utility views; router labels come from an automated VLM labeling pipeline. Real-world manipulation gains in efficiency and control performance (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: idea for choosing which input to fetch under a budget; VLM-labelled supervision precedent.

title: The Impact of Class Uncertainty Propagation in Perception-Based Motion Planning
relevance_note: MED — measures how upstream perception-uncertainty calibration affects closed-loop planning on nuPlan; supports the tool-noise-to-plan-quality link.
what: Compares two prediction-planning pipelines with different uncertainty propagation on nuPlan challenge scenarios; propagation generalizes better in complex closed-loop scenarios.
thesis_use: related work for noisy perception and calibration.

title: Sensor Query Schedule and Sensor Noise Covariances for Accuracy-constrained Trajectory Estimation
relevance_note: MED (LOW for method) — formal sensor-query-rate versus accuracy trade-off via semidefinite programs; vocabulary of query budget for state estimation, not planning.
what: Computes the sensor schedule or noise covariance needed for a target estimation accuracy, validated in simulation and real experiments; flags infeasible accuracy targets.
thesis_use: citation for query-budget framing only.

title: SafeDrive: Fine-Grained Safety Reasoning for End-to-End Driving in a Sparse World
relevance_note: MED — trajectory-conditioned world model plus agent-specific collision-risk evaluation, close to the "collision check against tracked actors" tool and to scoring candidates.
what: SWNet builds trajectory-conditioned sparse worlds of critical agents; FRNet scores agent-specific collision risk and drivable-area adherence. NAVSIM PDMS 91.6, EPDMS 87.5, 61 collisions out of 12,146 scenarios; Bench2Drive driving score 66.8%.
thesis_use: idea to borrow for the collision-check tool and ranker features.

title: PRAM-R: A Perception-Reasoning-Action-Memory Framework with LLM-Guided Modality Routing for Adaptive Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — selects which sensor modalities to run to cut cost, a scene-context (trajectory-agnostic) query-selection baseline in driving.
what: Asynchronous dual loop; an LLM router selects and weights modalities from environmental context and sensor diagnostics, with hysteresis stabilization. Abstract reports 87.2% fewer routing oscillations in synthetic stress tests, and on nuScenes 6.22% modality reduction with 20% memory recall at comparable trajectory accuracy to full-modality baselines.
thesis_use: related work for budgeted perception; contrast with candidate-conditioned selection (modest 6.22% saving shows little headroom for scene-only routing).

title: Risk-Aware Rulebooks for Multi-Objective Trajectory Evaluation under Uncertainty
relevance_note: MED — formalism to rank trajectories under uncertain environment responses, with a preorder guaranteeing consistent preferences; relevant to defining the oracle best candidate.
