what: Evaluates trajectories under the distribution of environment responses; proves a preorder; illustrated with a driving example (no empirical numbers).
thesis_use: oracle/ranking definition reference.

title: Knowing When to Ask: Resolving Uncertainty in Human-Robot Joint Planning via Explicit Dialogue and Implicit Intent Cues
relevance_note: MED — cost-optimal querying policy by dynamic programming so the robot asks only questions whose answers matter for the plan
what: Hypothesis-augmented A* enumerates traversability hypotheses and a DP computes the querying policy; cost-optimal clarification cuts interaction cost by 51.9% at 100% task success, and implicit intent reading cuts execution time by 25.4%. Gazebo plus UAV deployments.
thesis_use: closest "query only if the answer changes the plan" precedent (plan-conditioned querying), outside driving

title: Safe Probabilistic Planning for Human-Robot Interaction using Conformal Risk Control
relevance_note: MED — conformal risk control on CBF safety values, margins adjusted by interaction context
what: Combines control barrier functions with conformal risk control to bound constraint-violation probability around humans; on human-robot navigation it significantly reduces collision rates and safety violations versus baselines while keeping high success rates (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: calibration phase (context-adaptive safety margin)

title: Your Vision-Language-Action Model Already Has Attention Heads For Path Deviation Detection
relevance_note: MED — training-free monitor on a frozen VLA that triggers a cheap fallback policy.
what: Three attention heads out of over a thousand give a 44.6% deviation detection rate at 11.7% false positives; on detection the heavy VLA is bypassed for a lightweight RL shortest-path rollback on a physical robot (navigation).
thesis_use: example of detect-then-fallback with a frozen model; modest detection numbers.

title: TokenPB: Enabling VLA Action Self-Verification via VLM Token Probability Bucketing
relevance_note: MED — scores M sampled candidate actions and picks the best; theory on selection regret that separates candidate-set effects from calibration.
what: Co-trains a VLA with flow-matching loss and an auxiliary bucket-token loss; at inference samples M candidates, scores each by teacher-forced evaluation, selects the best, with KV-cache reuse. Reports success-rate gains over single-sample inference of +2.7 (simulation), +17.1 (real-world), +16.4 (out-of-distribution), and gains over external-verifier baselines under the same sampling budget.
thesis_use: related work for the ranker; the regret decomposition (candidate set vs calibration) supports the argument that candidate-set structure matters.

title: Shifting Uncertainty to Critical Moments: Towards Reliable Uncertainty Quantification for VLA Model
relevance_note: MED — failure prediction from uncertainty with max-pooling over windows so brief spikes are not diluted; relevant to calibrated accept/reject.
what: Max-based sliding-window pooling, motion-aware stability weighting, DoF-adaptive calibration via Bayesian optimization; improves failure prediction on LIBERO (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: idea for the calibration phase.

title: Utility-Guided Agent Orchestration for Efficient LLM Tool Use
relevance_note: MED — action selection among respond/retrieve/tool/verify/stop by estimated gain, step cost, uncertainty and redundancy
what: Treats orchestration as an explicit decision problem with a utility policy; compared with direct answering, threshold control, fixed workflows, ReAct and policy variants. The abstract states the aim is a controllable quality-cost framework, not best accuracy, and gives no numbers.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (gain minus cost minus redundancy utility form for the selector); baseline pattern

title: Uncertainty-Aware Vision-based Risk Object Identification via Conformal Risk Tube Prediction
relevance_note: MED — driving hazard identification with conformal coverage guarantees and a new multi-risk dataset
what: Conformal Risk Tube Prediction models spatiotemporal risk uncertainty with coverage guarantees for true risks and calibrated risk scores. A new dataset and metrics cover multi-risk scenario configurations and perception error propagation; it reduces nuisance braking alerts (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: benchmark / calibration-phase reference for conformal accept/reject on driving hazards

title: Collision-Aware Vision-Language Learning for End-to-End Driving with Multimodal Infraction Datasets
relevance_note: MED — collision prediction plug-in and a CARLA collision dataset; relates to the collision-check tool and hazard data.
what: VLAAD (MIL-based video-language anomaly detector) integrated into TransFuser++ gives a 14.12% relative driving-score increase on CARLA; on the new Real-Collide dashcam set a 0.6B VLAAD beats a multi-billion VLM by 23.3% AUC. Releases CARLA-Collide.
thesis_use: possible dataset/benchmark source and learned collision-risk baseline.

title: Effort-Based Criticality Metrics for Evaluating 3D Perception Errors in Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — scores perception errors by the braking/evasion effort they cause (decision-relevant error), which parallels deriving an oracle from consequences rather than detection accuracy.
what: False Speed Reduction, Maximum Deceleration Rate, Lateral Evasion Acceleration with reachability gate. On nuScenes and Argoverse 2, 65% to 93% of errors fall below the chosen criticality thresholds.
thesis_use: idea for "decision-relevant error" framing and tool-noise analysis.

title: Leveraging the Value of Information in POMDP Planning
relevance_note: MED — formal value-of-information (expected performance gain from reasoning about observations) varying over the belief space
what: A dynamic-programming framework processes observations conditionally on VOI per belief, and VOIMCP (an MCTS) skips observation branching when VOI is low. It has near-optimality guarantees and non-asymptotic convergence bounds; it outperforms baselines on several POMDP benchmarks.
thesis_use: theory citation for VOI as the quantity the selector should predict

title: Open-Loop Planning, Closed-Loop Verification: Speculative Verification for VLA
relevance_note: MED — lightweight verifier compares planned action to a closed-loop reference and triggers replanning only when needed; analogous to the future accept/replan policy.
what: Heavy VLA as low-frequency planner, light verifier monitors latest observations. Abstract gives no numbers.
thesis_use: idea for accept/replan trigger.

title: How Well Do Vision-Language Models Understand Sequential Driving Scenes? A Sensitivity Study
relevance_note: MED — measures how resolution, frame count, intervals and layout affect VLMs on driving scenes; informs zoom/crop value.
what: VENUSS compares 25+ VLMs over 2,600+ scenarios; top models reach 57% accuracy versus 65% for humans; VLMs do well on static object detection but poorly on vehicle dynamics and temporal relations.
thesis_use: supports why speed/distance tools help; a source for VLM-prompt design caveats.

title: Q-Zoom: Query-Aware Adaptive Perception for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models
relevance_note: MED — a learned gate decides whether high-resolution processing is needed, then a RoI is localised
what: A Dynamic Gating Network bypasses high-resolution processing when coarse features suffice; a Self-Distilled Region Proposal Network localises the RoI for demanding queries. Abstract is cut at fetch before the results; no numbers used.
thesis_use: analogue of the ROI tool plus gate; not driving

title: Temporal Difference Calibration in Sequential Tasks: Application to Vision-Language-Action Models
relevance_note: MED — sequential calibration of task-success confidence along an episode.
what: Defines a sequential Brier score whose risk minimizer equals the policy value function, so TD value estimation acts as a calibration mechanism. Improves on the prior state of the art on simulated and real-robot data; calibrated single-step action probabilities give competitive uncertainty estimates.
thesis_use: calibration-phase reference.

title: VLA-ATTC: Adaptive Test-Time Compute for VLA Models with Relative Action Critic Model
relevance_note: MED — uncertainty-based gate decides when to deliberate, then a pairwise critic picks the best of generated candidates; same gate-plus-candidate-critic structure, manipulation domain.
what: "Cognitive clutch" switches from reflexive execution to test-time compute; Relative Action Critic ranks candidates by pairwise comparison. On LIBERO-LONG it cuts the failure rate of PI0.5 by over 50%.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (pairwise relative ranker for the ranker stage).

title: Sentinel-VLA: A Metacognitive VLA Model with Active Status Monitoring for Dynamic Reasoning and Error Recovery
relevance_note: MED — reasons only when a monitor says so, minimizing compute; manipulation.
what: A sentinel module monitors execution and triggers reasoning at initial planning or on error detection; data auto-generated (44 tasks, over 2.6 million transitions). Real-world success up over 30% versus PI0.
thesis_use: related work for on-demand reasoning triggers.

title: Non-Myopic Active Feature Acquisition via Pathwise Policy Gradients
relevance_note: MED — active feature acquisition: choose which costly feature to acquire per instance and when to stop
what: A continuous relaxation enables pathwise policy gradients through the full acquisition trajectory, with a straight-through rollout that matches discrete deployment and a variance bound motivating staged temperature sharpening. Better than state-of-the-art AFA baselines on synthetic and real datasets.
thesis_use: related-work framing (selector as an AFA policy); non-myopic extension if multi-step queries are ever allowed

title: GuardAD: Safeguarding Autonomous Driving MLLMs via Markovian Safety Logic
relevance_note: MED — model-agnostic safeguard that infers latent hazards and revises actions of a driving MLLM.
what: Neuro-symbolic Markovian logic states infer emerging and latent hazards; Logic-Driven Action Revision refines actions without changing the MLLM. Accident rates fall by 32.07% and task performance rises 6.85%, with closed-loop and physical vehicle studies.
thesis_use: related work for the accept/replan stage.

title: C-CoT: Counterfactual Chain-of-Thought with Vision-Language Models for Safe Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — VLM evaluates consequences of alternative meta-action combinations in a tree before planning.
what: Five-stage CoT (scene, critical objects, risk, counterfactual risk, plan) with a meta-action evaluation tree, fine-tuned on Qwen2.5-VL-7B with LoRA on DeepAccident-CCoT. Risk prediction recall 81.9%, collision rate 3.52%, L2 error 1.98 m.
thesis_use: competitor-style VLM-only candidate-action critic; contrast with tool-based inspection.

title: Think as Needed: Geometry-Driven Adaptive Perception for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED. Scene-complexity-triggered shallow/deep perception routing, i.e. a trajectory-agnostic compute trigger.
what: Enhanced HOPE measures the geometric complexity of each LiDAR frame without labels and routes it through a shallow or deep path, with a memory module for occluded objects. On nuScenes and CARLA it cuts latency 38% on simple scenes with no accuracy loss, adds 2.7 mAP on rare long-tail scenarios, and tracks objects through occlusions longer than 5 seconds.
thesis_use: example competitor for the "scene-uncertainty" baseline family (scene-level routing, no candidate conditioning).

title: CADS: Conformal Adaptive Decision System for Cost-Efficient Image Classification
relevance_note: MED — conformal uncertainty routes samples through a model cascade, cost up to 12 times lower than heavy-model inference
what: Sequential multi-model routing from lightweight "Scout" to high-capacity "Oracle" models, validated on two (clinical) datasets.
thesis_use: scene-uncertainty cascade baseline pattern

title: Model-Adaptive Tool Necessity Reveals the Knowing-Doing Gap in LLM Tool Use
relevance_note: MED — defines tool necessity empirically per model and measures the gap between need and calls
what: Necessity is defined from each model's own performance; across four models on arithmetic and factual QA, necessity and observed tool-call behaviour mismatch by 26.5-54.0% and 30.8-41.8% respectively. Hidden-state probes show both "belief" and "action" signals are linearly decodable but nearly orthogonal in late-layer last-token directions.
thesis_use: supports the "VLM mostly says none" finding; the per-model-necessity definition parallels per-noise-level expected gain

title: Vision-Based Runtime Monitoring under Varying Specifications using Semantic Latent Representations
relevance_note: MED — conformally certified monitor from images with finite-sample guarantees, checked on Waymo data
what: A reusable monitor predicts atom robustness scores of past-time signal temporal logic from images under partial observability; one conformal calibration pass certifies a whole formula fragment. On a pedestrian-crossroad benchmark the semantic-basis monitor is up to 4 times tighter at long horizons; both monitors meet empirical coverage on Waymo driving data.
thesis_use: idea to borrow for the future accept/fallback phase (certified monitor on perceptual inputs)

title: CLOVER: Closed-Loop Value Estimation and Ranking for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Planning
relevance_note: MED. Generator-scorer planner that ranks candidate trajectories by predicted planning sub-scores, so it is a reference for the ranker stage.
what: A generator proposes diverse candidate trajectories and a scorer predicts planning-metric sub-scores to rank them. Training uses evaluator-filtered pseudo-expert trajectories and closed-loop self-distillation toward teacher-selected top-k and Pareto targets. Reports 94.5 PDMS and 90.4 EPDMS on NAVSIM and 48.3 EPDMS on the NavHard split.
thesis_use: related work for the ranker and for "scorer quality limits proposal selection"; idea to borrow is the oracle-best-by-evaluator target.

title: R2V Agent: Teaching SLMs When to Ask for Help
relevance_note: MED — calibrated step-level router that escalates only when residual failure risk warrants it, reported as a reliability-cost frontier
what: A distilled small-model policy, a teacher LLM, a process verifier scoring candidate actions each step and a router trained with Brier-calibrated probabilities and a CVaR-constrained objective. On HumanEval+ it reaches 94.3% success with 0.60% LLM escalation; on TextWorld it recovers from 64.6% to 98.2% at 41.7% escalation; on TerminalBench 93.3% at 33.9% LLM calls, about half the heuristic-router cost.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (accuracy vs. escalation-rate frontier; verifier scoring candidate actions resembles the ranker); not driving

title: Is VLA Reasoning Faithful? Probing Safety of Chain-of-Causation in Autonomous Driving Models
relevance_note: MED — shows a driving VLA misses pedestrians and is fragile, which motivates tool checks.
what: 300 Alpamayo-R1-10B inferences over 100 PhysicalAI-AV scenarios: reasoning fidelity 42.5%, 94 missed pedestrians in one third of pedestrian-relevant scenes, 97.7% trajectory fragility under mild perturbations, 48.3% mean reasoning-action consistency.
thesis_use: motivation citation for why perception tools are needed.

title: Bench2Drive-Robust: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Autonomous Driving under Deployment Perturbations
relevance_note: MED. Perturbation benchmark for E2E driving that is analogous to the project's tool-noise levels, but perturbs the planner's inputs, not the tools.
what: Closed-loop benchmark of camera-stream failures (frame drop, partial observation), ego-state errors (GPS noise, speed/odometry error) and model inference delay. Evaluates representative E2E methods at several severities and reports substantial closed-loop degradation (no numbers in the abstract).
thesis_use: related work for noise-severity design; contrasts with the open-loop protocol used here.

title: Reason--Imagine--Act: Closed-Loop LLM Decision Making with World Models for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED. LLM proposes an action template and candidate sub-actions, a world model rolls them out, a safety scorer picks one: a candidate-then-verify loop.
what: Per step the LLM proposes candidates, a world model does short-horizon rollouts and a safety scorer selects the safest executable action, with feedback to the next reasoning step. In a CARLA point-goal protocol (1000 episodes) RIA reaches 80.05% route completion, 51.10% arrival rate and 0.20% collision rate, ahead of training-free baselines CARLA TM and MADA.
thesis_use: related work for candidate verification with a learned model as the "tool"; no query-budget notion.

title: Pre-VLA: Preemptive Runtime Verification for Reliable Vision-Language-Action and World-Model Rollouts
relevance_note: MED — predicts safety confidence and advantage for candidate action chunks before execution, with a resampling scheduler under a computation budget.
what: A multimodal backbone with a dual-branch head predicts safety confidence and critic-derived advantage per candidate chunk; trained with Focal classification, advantage regression and soft-threshold calibration; a dual-mode scheduler filters low-quality actions and triggers adaptive resampling under a limited compute budget. On LIBERO, average closed-loop success rises from 30.79% to 37.62% over RynnVLA-002, with 183.9 ms average forward verification time per chunk.
thesis_use: related work for accept/reject of candidates and budgeted re-querying; a model for the accept/replan policy in the future phase.

title: RECTOR: Priority-Aware Rule-Based Reranking for Compliance-Aware Autonomous Driving Trajectory Selection
relevance_note: MED. Selects one trajectory from a K=6 candidate set with a tiered rule scorer and tests against corrupted confidence.
what: A post-generation reranker scores candidates against a Safety > Legal > Road > Comfort rulebook and selects lexicographically, without retraining the predictor. On Waymo Open Motion Dataset validation_interactive (43,219 augmented instances) it cuts Safety+Legal violations from 28.58% to 20.42% and Total from 40.32% to 32.41% versus confidence-only. Under adversarial confidence corruption, confidence-only fails in 100% of scenarios while the rule-aware selectors reject the injected mode in about 96%. Authors say results are proxy-evaluator, open-loop.
thesis_use: candidate-set selection baseline or ranker alternative; the rule tiers could define an oracle-best candidate; open-loop proxy caveat matches the project's setting.

title: When Does Adaptive Guidance Help? Belief-Aware Privileged Distillation for Autonomous Driving Under Partial Observability
relevance_note: MED. Finds that ensemble disagreement does not detect missing information under occlusion.
what: BA-GSAC modulates the privileged-distillation coefficient by ensemble disagreement; tested on Highway-Env at three POMDP levels. Under severe occlusion (3 seeds) the coefficient collapses to its minimum within about 3K steps, because the ensemble models only what is visible. A linear-decay schedule performed best in severe POMDP (mean 116.5, CV=8.9%). The authors mark their proposed fix as not validated.
thesis_use: supporting argument that scene-uncertainty triggers are blind to occluded hazards; weak evidence (RL, small seeds).

title: Knowing When to Ask: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for LLM Tool Use
relevance_note: MED — learns which individual tool call helped, penalising unnecessary calls
what: CARL trains a critic on the model's own rollouts to learn where parametric knowledge suffices and where external help is needed, assigning independent credit per tool-use segment from a single binary outcome.
thesis_use: idea to borrow for per-call credit (the project's expected-gain label is a per-tool counterfactual of this kind)

title: VLAConf: Calibrated Task-Success Confidence for Vision-Language-Action Models
relevance_note: MED — calibrated confidence from frozen VLA representations, used to trigger expert handoff.
what: A step-conditioned Coin-Flip Network gives an uncalibrated score, and a low-capacity calibrator fitted on outcome-labelled rollouts maps it to task-success probability. Improves online confidence estimation on LIBERO, and confidence-triggered handoffs improve success over no intervention.
thesis_use: calibration-phase reference (frozen features plus a small calibrator; confidence-triggered deferral). No conformal guarantee.

title: Uncertainty-Aware and Temporally Regulated Expert Advice in Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED. Requests expert help when epistemic or aleatoric uncertainty exceeds adaptive thresholds, within an advice budget.
what: Commitment-cooldown and stochastic early-stop regulate duration and frequency of guidance; built on an IQN backbone in CARLA unsignalized intersections. Improves success by 5-7% over the IQN baseline.
thesis_use: defer/ask-for-help trigger example; trigger is uncertainty-only, like the scene-uncertainty baseline.

title: Does Visual Information Play a Decisive Role in Vision-Language-Action Model Driving Behavior?
relevance_note: MED — structured visual perturbations (channel, information, structure level) on driving VLAs, open-loop and closed-loop.
what: Finds evaluation-dependent dependency patterns and uneven visual grounding across abstraction levels (no numbers in the abstract).
thesis_use: guidance for the sensor-perturbation and noise-level design.

title: Probing Collision Grounding in Vision-Language Models for Safe Human-Robot Collaboration
relevance_note: MED — VLMs are weak at present and imminent collision judgement, relevant to the collision-check tool and to VLM-as-selector expectations
what: TouchSafeBench has 2,940 simulated indoor episodes in Habitat 3.0 with multi-view RGB-D and simulator contact labels. Across three VLMs and nine visual representations the best average Macro-F1 stays below 50%; explicit depth does not automatically become collision evidence.
thesis_use: supports why geometric tools beat VLM judgement; indoor, not driving

title: Safe2Drive: Evaluating Safe Driving Behaviors of E2E Autonomous Driving Models
relevance_note: MED. Hazard benchmark with an occluded-VRU family, which is one of the project's three hazard types.
what: 100 Bench2Drive-aligned scenarios in three families (work zones, pedestrian jaywalking, occluded vulnerable road users) plus a SafeDriving Score. LEAD falls from 94.70 DS on Bench2Drive to 39.95 on S2D, and SimLingo from 85.07 to 41.00; SDS is 11.85 and 15.27.
thesis_use: citation for "occlusion hazards break current planners"; scenario-design reference for the MetaDrive hazards.

title: Do Multimodal Agents Really Benefit from Tool Use? A Systematic Study of Capability Gains
relevance_note: MED — evidence that tool access adds little beyond tool-free settings
what: Studies Thyme and DeepEyesV2 against tool-free and pure-text counterparts; 93% of DeepEyesV2's tool-solved problems and 96% of Thyme's are also solved by a non-tool setting, and tool access does not reliably cut token cost.
thesis_use: caution and motivation for measuring counterfactual tool gain (the oracle-selector Pareto) rather than tool-call counts

title: Distribution-Free Risk-Aware Planning and Control Under Uncertainty Using Conformal Spectral Risk Control
relevance_note: MED — conformal risk control extended to spectral risk measures inside an MPC planner, simulated vehicle obstacle avoidance
what: Prediction sets guarantee spectral-risk constraint satisfaction without distributional assumptions and are used in risk-aware MPC; improved safety and reduced solve time versus a baseline RA-MPC in simulated vehicle obstacle avoidance (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: calibration phase (risk-controlled plan acceptance)

title: Uncertainty-Aware Clarification in LLM Agents with Information Gain
relevance_note: MED. Trains a clarifier with an Information Gain Reward (Bayesian belief update toward the true goal), which is a value-of-information target for deciding what to ask.
what: Evaluated in a clarification-enhanced tau-Bench with five backbones; success improves 3.7% over the no-clarification baseline with 0.3 extra interaction steps on average.
thesis_use: idea to borrow for the expected-gain label; not driving.

title: Bridging Predictive Uncertainty and Safe Action: Sample-Conditioned Differentiable Planning for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED. Diffusion-sampled futures feed a differentiable planner with an empirical CVaR tail-risk constraint.
what: Not conformal, but a risk-constrained planner over sampled scenarios, plus a directed-graph scene representation. Validation numbers were cut off in the fetched abstract view, so none are quoted.
thesis_use: related work for the future risk-control phase.

title: Conformal Risk-Averse Decision Making with Action Conditional Guarantee
relevance_note: MED — guarantees conditioned on the action taken, which fits per-candidate accept/reject
what: Introduces action-conditional conformal prediction, shows the sets act as a proxy for the feasible decision space for risk-averse decision makers optimising action-conditional value-at-risk, and gives a finite-sample pinball-loss algorithm. Experiments on two real-world datasets improve action-conditional performance over conformal baselines.
thesis_use: calibration phase (guarantee per chosen candidate rather than marginal)

title: Mission-Level Runtime Assurance Framework for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — driving runtime monitor that rejects unsafe or mission-infeasible commands before execution.
what: Extends highway-env with mission-level fault scenarios and a runtime monitor, compared with an adapted Simplex-Drive baseline. Platform-level runtime safety alone misses mission-level faults, while the proposed monitor rejects mission-infeasible commands and improves mission success.
thesis_use: related work for accept/reject-and-fallback in driving; no calibration guarantee.

title: Co-GLANCE: Uncertainty-Aware Active Perception for Heterogeneous Robot Teaming
relevance_note: MED — calibrated (conformal) uncertainty with abstention directly triggers which robot acquires a new viewpoint to resolve occlusion
what: Distils a VLM into an end-to-end model for occlusion segmentation and robot allocation; conformal prediction with selective abstention gives coverage guarantees for segmentation, allocation and detection, and these estimates trigger active perception. Outperforms cloud VLM baselines in occlusion segmentation (rest of the abstract truncated at fetch; UNVERIFIED beyond that).
thesis_use: related work for "calibrated uncertainty triggers acquisition" (scene-uncertainty-style trigger with guarantees); occlusion theme

title: Where Does the Answer Come From? Benchmarking View-Level Visual Evidence Identification in Multi-View MLLMs for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — a small benchmark where the model must pick which camera view supports the answer; a query-selection analogue.
what: 122 conflict-centric QA pairs from 73 nuScenes scenes, evaluated for camera-view selection, oracle-view QA and joint prediction (no results in the abstract).
thesis_use: related benchmark for "where to look"; tiny.

title: VeriSpace: Spatially Grounded Action Verification for Vision-Language-Action Models
relevance_note: MED — test-time verifier that discriminates between subtle candidate actions using 3D-injected scene encoding.
what: A 3D-aware verifier with Dual-Path 3D-Injected Scene Encoding and Spatially-Grounded Action Reasoning that evaluates each candidate for spatial relations, geometric validity and goal progress. Reported to improve decision reliability over the base VLA policies and prior verification methods (no numbers in the abstract).
thesis_use: related work (candidate verifier); a possible ranker comparison if geometry features are added.

title: ScoutVLA: UAV-Centric Active Perception via a Dual-Expert VLA Model for Open-World Embodied Question Answering
relevance_note: MED — an evidence-driven active perception policy that first infers which evidence is missing, then moves to get it.
what: Introduces FG-EQA (over 40K simulated and 1K real-world trajectories) and a dual-expert VLA: a vision-language expert infers missing evidence, a flow-matching action expert generates viewpoint-refinement trajectories. Reports 10.48x higher average strict success rate and 7.72x higher average QA correctness than baselines.
thesis_use: related work on active perception; not a tool selector and no query budget.

title: LIBERO-Occ: Evaluating and Improving Vision-Language-Action Models under Scene-Induced Occlusion via Viewpoint Imagination
relevance_note: MED — occlusion benchmark with types and severity levels (manipulation, not driving).
what: State-of-the-art VLAs degrade substantially under occlusion; Viewpoint Imagination generates a complementary view and conditions action on observed plus imagined evidence.
thesis_use: design reference for occlusion types and severities.

title: Self-Supervised Relevance Modelling in Autonomous Driving via Counterfactual Analysis
relevance_note: MED. Learns which objects matter for the AV's decisions via counterfactual removal, to focus perception compute.
what: A relevance model is trained self-supervised on a synthetic causal dataset in one urban scenario and estimates object relevance with millisecond-level latency. Relevance heatmaps are proposed as proactive inputs to perception and planning.
thesis_use: idea to borrow for decision-relevance labels; complements the "expected gain" targets.
code: abstract says the dataset and model are openly released (URL not in the fetched text)

title: Elastic Queries Reinforcement Learning: Self-Aware Policy Execution for VLA Models
relevance_note: MED. Learns, per query, how much compute and how long an open-loop chunk to use, under an amortized NFE budget. It is manipulation, not driving.
what: A latent-schedule adaptor picks latent input, denoising budget and chunk length without fine-tuning the VLA. A critic ensemble's disagreement gives a state difficulty signal. Reduces amortized inference cost while preserving or improving task success, across simulation and real-robot manipulation.
thesis_use: example of a disagreement-based scene-difficulty trigger under a budget; fits the scene-uncertainty baseline family.

title: MuseVLA: An Adaptive Multimodal Sensing Vision-Language-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation
relevance_note: MED — selects which sensor to invoke and what to attend to, framed as a tool call with arguments.
what: Generates a sensor token and target description from instruction and visual context, then converts the chosen sensor reading into a grounded sensor image for fusion and action generation. Real-robot dexterous tasks (temperature-guided pick-and-place, audio-driven search, radar-assisted retrieval) reach 80.6% average success, above RGB-only and multisensory VLA baselines.
thesis_use: related work for "which sensor/tool to call"; contrast: selection is conditioned on instruction and image, not on candidate actions, and has no budget or noise analysis.

title: Zero-Shot Active Feature Acquisition via LLM-Elicitation
relevance_note: MED — LLM supplies priors, a separate model decides acquisition
what: The LLM is asked only for unary deviations and pairwise co-variations (sufficient statistics of a Markov random field) and acquisition is planned over that model, for binary classification and top-k identification.
thesis_use: contrast case: do not let the LLM decide, let it supply statistics (consistent with the frozen-VLM-as-feature-source result)

title: VLA-FAIL: Efficient Task Failure Detection for Finetuned Vision-Language-Action Models
relevance_note: MED — cheap runtime failure detection that needs no failure data; detection accuracy versus latency metric.
what: Combines last-layer Mahalanobis distance (out-of-distribution states) with action chunk consistency across receding-horizon chunks, and introduces AUCPDT, which jointly scores precision, recall and detection time. The combination frequently beats more expensive baselines in real-world and simulation tests.
thesis_use: trigger signals for the fallback branch in the future phase; AUCPDT as a metric idea.

title: Assistron: Bayesian Shared Autonomy with Off-the-shelf Vision-Language-Action Models
relevance_note: MED — decides when to ask the human to intervene (phase-aware detection), without fine-tuning the VLA.
what: Prioritizes human intervention at critical failure points and adjusts VLA actions through flow-matching guidance; improves success over pure autonomous baselines on a multi-task scene recovery benchmark (no numbers in the abstract).
thesis_use: weak related work on deferral.

title: Intend, Reflect, Refine: An Adaptive Multimodal Reflection Framework for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED. VLA that picks its reasoning mode by scene complexity and reflects on a preliminary intent before the final trajectory.
what: IRR-Drive writes a textual intention, predicts future semantic BEV, then refines the trajectory; an adaptive reflection reward lets the model choose its reasoning mode by scene complexity. The abstract claims state-of-the-art PDMS and EPDMS on NAVSIM (no numbers in the fetched text).
thesis_use: think-vs-look switching competitor in the DriveAgent-R1 family; trigger is scene-based.

title: A Query-Driven Communication-Efficient Digital Twins Design for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED. A digital twin actively requests environment data from the vehicle based on its own simulation result, under a communication constraint.
what: Formulates minimizing planning position error under fidelity and communication limits, with a cross-time-step progressive query mechanism. Reports a 24% lower planning position error versus traditional methods and 40% lower communication overhead.
thesis_use: conceptually a budgeted, simulation-conditioned query; wireless setting, so only an analogy.

title: RouterVLA: Budgeted Commissioning and Expert Onboarding for Growing VLA Pools
relevance_note: MED (weak) — chooses which expert to deploy under an exactly cost-matched probe budget.
what: Reaches 60.53% held-out success, +1.64 points over a semantic shortlist, at a matched probe budget.
thesis_use: tangential example of budget-matched selection.

title: LWDrive: Layer-Wise World-Model-Guided Vision-Language Model Planning for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — expands a diverse candidate set around a VLM plan, refines it, and a score head selects the best trajectory.
what: Foresight Cascade Planner refines candidates with future-frame supervision, history, action queries and multi-view BEV features; a score head selects the final trajectory. Scores 92.0 on NAVSIM and 89.6 on NAVSIM-v2.
thesis_use: related work for trajectory scorer over candidate sets; no tool calls.

title: Look Before You Leap: Distilling Tree Search into Action Evaluation for Frozen VLA Models
relevance_note: MED — candidate-action evaluator over a frozen policy with uncertainty-regularized Q; manipulation, not driving.
what: A frozen VLA proposes multiple candidates and a distilled lightweight Q-model picks the highest uncertainty-regularized one. Real-robot average success rises from 42.8% to 55.6%; pass@k on frozen VLAs goes from 33% (pass@1) to 92% (pass@32).
thesis_use: idea (propose-then-evaluate with frozen backbone; oracle-best-of-k as upper bound).

title: What Do They See? Interpreting Complex Road Scenarios Through the Eyes of Vision-Language-Action Models for Safe and Trustworthy Autonomous Vehicle Learning
relevance_note: MED — measures each object's causal effect on the planned trajectory by inpainting it out; the same notion as decision-relevance of a query target.
what: Counterfactual ablation on Alpamayo 1 over 210 nuScenes scenes builds Counter-nuScenes. Vehicles and pedestrians on the path dominate. Traffic lights exert disproportionate effect relative to image footprint. Some irrelevant objects still move the plan.
thesis_use: evidence that the traffic-light and in-path actor hazards are the decision-relevant ones; possible recipe for oracle labels from real data.

title: Cognitive Dual-Process Planning for Autonomous Driving with Structured Scene Knowledge and Verifiable Reasoning-Action Consistency
relevance_note: MED — a lightweight visual Arbiter from encoder features routes to fast vs slow reasoning (decides whether to spend compute).
what: Arbiter estimates scene complexity before decoding. On 574 verified NAVSIM samples: 80.14% planning accuracy, 97.20% LCS, 17.39% lower average latency than always slow reasoning.
thesis_use: baseline family (trajectory-agnostic complexity trigger from frozen encoder features).

title: When Should Active RAG Retrieve? A Budget-Aware Evaluation of Utility, Calibration, and Cost
relevance_note: MED — evaluation methodology: retrieval is valuable only through its marginal correctness change over no-retrieval; exact top-k utility frontiers, calibrated threshold frontiers, conservative budget frontiers.
what: Argues single-point comparisons conflate a looser budget with a better policy; separates whether trigger scores rank useful decisions, whether thresholds calibrated on past data meet future budgets, and trigger-side cost.
thesis_use: evaluation protocol to borrow (report realized budget, not nominal; oracle top-k frontier as the upper bound on the Pareto plot).

title: Look Where It Matters: Adaptive Visual Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Models
relevance_note: MED — uncertainty-gated crop-and-re-encode, the same pattern as a scene-uncertainty ROI trigger, in manipulation.
what: AtVLA adds register tokens and uncertainty-gated local refinement. The action expert samples multiple action chunks and uses their disagreement as uncertainty. Only for uncertain steps, a region chosen by action-conditioned attention rollout is cropped and re-encoded at high resolution. LIBERO success rises from 94.2% to 98.4% and real-world success from 46.5% to 69.0%. Cropping triggers on about 30% of replanning steps at 1.4-1.6x compute.
thesis_use: baseline-style precedent for uncertainty-triggered ROI inspection; note its trigger uses disagreement among sampled action chunks, which is a weak form of candidate-set dependence.

title: BRiG-AFA: Bellman Risk-to-Go Learning for Non-Myopic Active Feature Acquisition
relevance_note: MED — "candidate-conditioned risk-to-go function for every remaining budget", supervised alternative to RL for budgeted acquisition.
what: Learns a separate candidate-conditioned risk-to-go function per remaining budget, fitted backward with Bellman targets from the one-step terminal classification risk; inference greedily minimizes the learned risk. Fashion-MNIST with 20 candidate pixels: +10.20 +/- 0.74 points at four acquisitions; mean paired gain across budgets {2,4,8,12,16} is 3.50 +/- 0.37 points. Three-seed MiniBooNE mixed at small budgets. Tabular/pixel features, not perception tools.
thesis_use: idea to borrow if we move beyond one-step (we allow only one call, so non-myopic gains do not apply); cite as AFA context.

title: SAFECAST: Robust Failure Detection for VLA Policies with Contrast-Set Training and Calibration
relevance_note: MED — hidden-state risk probes with functional conformal prediction, calibration under deployment shift (manipulation).
what: Contrast-set perturbations (visual and language) augment probe training and calibration; improves failure-detection ROC-AUC over the baseline on DROID (real) and LIBERO (sim). Sim-to-real calibration beat real-only rollouts.
thesis_use: idea for the conformal accept/reject phase; calibration under shift.

title: OpenVisTool: An Open Recipe for Synthesizing Instructive Visual Tool-Use Trajectories
relevance_note: MED — argues tool-call supervision should be kept only if the tool observation causally contributes to the answer; generic multimodal, not driving.
what: Framework retains a trajectory only if the answer is correct and the tool observations causally contribute. Builds OpenVisTool-42K and OpenVisTool-Bench over five visual reasoning domains. Fine-tuning four backbones (4B-27B) improves visual tool use and two out-of-distribution benchmarks.
thesis_use: supports the expected-gain labeling idea (label a tool call by its counterfactual contribution rather than by final correctness).

title: ToolVision: Learning When and How to Use Visual Tools with Capability-Aligned Supervision
relevance_note: MED — RL reward for tool use only on questions where tools give clear benefit (compares with and without tools).
what: SFT trajectories are ranked by committee-scored stepwise evidence gain; before RL, the learner is compared with and without tools and tool use is rewarded only where it clearly helps. Image VQA, not driving.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (with/without-tool benefit as the training signal); abstract was truncated in my read, so no headline numbers recorded.

title: Calibrated Predictive Safety for Heterogeneous Robots: An Action-Conditioned JEPA Framework with Model-Based Safety Shields
relevance_note: MED — K candidate action chunks scored by calibrated risk and progress heads, with a shield and fallback ladder; manipulation, but same decision structure as the future phase.
what: Proposer gives K candidates; an action-conditioned JEPA rolls each out in a frozen-encoder latent space; calibrated heads score them; a deterministic shield filters inadmissible candidates; a fallback ladder handles empty sets. In 600-episode LIBERO-Long configurations it improved success over a shield-only baseline and reduced collision false negatives at matched recall.
thesis_use: idea to borrow for the accept/replan/fallback phase and for frozen-encoder candidate scoring.

title: Learning to Look Again: Loss-Gap Supervision for Free-form Crop Routing in Vision-Language Models
relevance_note: MED — learned router for whether to take an extra look, trained on offline "did the extra view help" labels.
what: GapSight compares answer loss or option margin under a global view and crop-augmented views; helpful crops become labels, distilled into a one-shot router that predicts whether to review, expected utility and a crop box. On InternVL2.5-8B the six-benchmark average rises from 52.25 to 64.29, above CropVLM (57.16), ViCrop (55.84), ZoomRefine (54.43).
thesis_use: idea to borrow (label construction from counterfactual with/without-tool outcome); comparable to expected-gain targets.

title: Variance-Guided Spatial Attention Fusion for Robust End-to-End Driving under Asymmetric Sensor Degradation
relevance_note: MED — calibrated per-pixel reliability and a waypoint uncertainty scale that flags severe degradation.
what: Physically grounded augmentor, heteroscedastic reliability maps, cross-modal trust softmax; improves closed-loop driving score, route completion and infraction score on CARLA Longest6 (no numbers in abstract).
thesis_use: noise-model idea for tool-noise levels; uncertainty signal for a trigger baseline.

title: Gating Before Commitment: Anticipating Intent Divergence to Prevent Post-Interaction Decision Failures in Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — gate on the planned maneuver before commitment, with uncertainty treated as abstention.
what: Intent-geometry divergence score gates the plan; fires 72 ms after drift onset, 161 ms before corridor exit, in all ten replays. Treating uncertainty as abstention cut false triggers from nine in 5.9 min to 0.341 per minute. Very small evidence base (five clips).
thesis_use: weak idea for abstention/fallback phase.

title: When Does Corruption Break the Plan? A Degradation-Tolerance Benchmark for Camera-Only End-to-End Driving
relevance_note: MED — sensor-perturbation benchmark at the planning-output level.
what: 16 corruption families at 5 severities, 15 policies, open-loop nuScenes/NAVSIM plus CARLA closed-loop anchor. Blur, JPEG and raindrop damage planning most; a released VLA planner loses only 11.5% when all six cameras are blinded.
thesis_use: benchmark idea for tool-noise levels; shows ego-status shortcut risk.

title: From Proxy Learning to Driving Decisions: A Transfer-Based Framework for Evaluating Future-Aware Autonomous Driving Planners
relevance_note: MED — evaluation methodology for proposal-based planners; separates support (is the best candidate present) from selection regret.
what: Decision-Transfer Decomposition (score margins, switch-conditioned utility, support-vs-selection regret) and a reliability-constrained validation. On NAVSIM-v1, component BCE falls from 0.705 to 0.530 while held selected PDM falls from 0.963 to 0.961.
thesis_use: evaluation idea (report regret vs oracle candidate, paired bootstrap for small gains).

title: Worst-Case Hidden-Vehicle Trajectory Search in Spatiotemporal Occlusion Regions
relevance_note: MED — occlusion hazard generation: worst-case legal hidden-vehicle trajectories against the ego plan.
what: Bilevel minimax search over certified hidden-state modes; on eight Waymo Open Motion Dataset scenarios, identifies six avoidable counterexamples; visibility-memory horizon K=1 to K=20 cuts retained hidden seeds by 18.45% (total).
thesis_use: idea for adversarial occlusion hazards in MetaDrive.

title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Counterfactual Diagnosis of End-to-End and VLA Driving Policies Under Domain Shift
relevance_note: MED — counterfactual edits (pedestrian removed, relit) test whether plans respond to hazards.
what: Six released policies, 246 NAVSIM near-pedestrian scenes; when the pedestrian lies on the planned path only 1.9% of responses are genuine avoidance, with median clearance change at most 0.03 m.
thesis_use: benchmark idea; evidence that planners ignore hazards, motivating perception queries.

title: Risk-Aware Online Conformal State Probing
relevance_note: MED — conformal guarantee on whether to probe, with cost (probing rate) minimized.
what: Online conformal state probing (OCSP) is a joint action and probing policy that provably controls the missed query error (fraction of instances where probing would have been beneficial) while minimizing probing rate; works with pre-trained value-based policies without retraining. Validated in numerical simulation only.
thesis_use: idea to borrow for calibrated tool-call decisions in the future phase.

title: Auditing Latent-Space Monitors for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — failure monitors from model latents; relevant to frozen-feature gains and runtime failure prediction.
what: On LaneSegNet and VAD, latent probes reach AUROC 0.780 (map) and 0.868 (VAD mean-ADE), but output-only monitors reach 0.825 and 0.924 (ego state, command and predicted trajectory for VAD); adding latents gives no statistically resolved gain.
thesis_use: contradicts/cautions the value of embeddings; add an outputs-only control; failure monitor for the future phase.

title: LAVOIR: Teaching a Single-Pass Decision Encoder When and What to Ask with Amortized Value of Information
relevance_note: MED — amortized expected-gain targets for which query to make, learned in one forward pass; text domain.
what: Candidate missing-info slots are placed next to the answer options; one pass returns the decision distribution and, per slot, the expected gain in correct-decision probability. Labels come from realized gains averaged over profiles; a Gini cap bounds predicted value. Policy matches a greedy oracle VOI policy (AUC 0.799 vs 0.797); with at most 0.5 questions per conversation it is 14.1 points more accurate than never asking.
thesis_use: idea to borrow (expected-gain regression, oracle-VOI comparison, cap on predicted value); parallel to the MLP selector.

title: CausalDriveBench: Evaluating Causal Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED/LOW — distinguishes causally active, dormant and distractor entities; includes alternative-trajectory evaluation.
what: 7,285 verified causal QA pairs and 1,000 counterfactual trajectories on nuScenes. Evaluates 10 driving VLAs and 3 VLMs. Best QA accuracy is 70.6%, and QA accuracy and trajectory accuracy are statistically uncorrelated across models.
thesis_use: related benchmark; the active/dormant/distractor split parallels decision-relevant versus merely salient objects.

title: CAR-VLA: Complexity-Aware and Risk-Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — driving VLA that chooses a reasoning mode from scene complexity and dynamic risk (whether/how to think).
what: Maps four complexity-risk categories to three modes (Fast Intuition, Slow Thinking, Reflex Response) via supervised training then RL. NAVSIM v1 91.1 PDMS, NAVSIM v2 90.3 EPDMS, Navhard 35.0 EPDMS.
thesis_use: baseline family for trajectory-agnostic triggering (scene-uncertainty/risk), alongside DriveAgent-R1.

relevance_note: MED — explains why a depth/speed tool is needed and why frozen hidden states beat verbal output.

For ego speed, continuous probes reach 4.7-5.8 km/h MAE versus 10.2-16.8 km/h for verbal outputs. Surrounding-agent speed is weakly encoded, and multiple frames give inconsistent verbal gains.
thesis_use: motivation for the distance/speed tool and for probing embeddings with a head rather than prompting.

title: World4Scorer: Outcome-Grounded World Modeling for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — generate-and-select scorer that predicts a per-candidate state and uses simulator outcome labels for unexecuted candidates.

thesis_use: parallels our oracle labels from privileged simulator state; candidate-conditioned ranker reference.

title: ExceptionDrive: A Planning-Oriented Counterfactual Corner-Case Benchmark for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — hazard-insertion benchmark with reference-free planning metrics; plus a VLM Reminder Agent for hazard records.
what: Inserts hazards into real nuScenes scenes (21 tasks, six safety families); metrics UR, HCC, HPR, CTS; seven planners often intrude into hazard regions. Reminder Agent improves strategy accuracy and reduces under-warning zero-shot.

title: Towards Reliable Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — evaluates Qwen3.5-9B (the project's frozen VLM) for accuracy and confidence reliability under visual corruption.
what: Evaluates five VLMs (Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma4-E4B, LLaVA-OneVision-7B, DriveFusionQA-4B, Alpamayo-1.5-10B) on four driving QA datasets under degraded inputs. Effects of corruption vary across models, datasets and input settings. Applies Visual Evidence Augmentation, which helps for some model and dataset pairs but not consistently.
thesis_use: supports the noise-level design and VLM-confidence caveats; citation for why prompting the VLM to choose tools is unreliable.

title: Learning to Ask: Information Acquisition for SLM-LLM Collaboration, under a budget
relevance_note: MED — learns whether to call an external advisor, how to formulate the query, under an API budget; performance-cost tradeoff vs routing baselines.
what: Three-stage RLVR framework; improves the performance-cost tradeoff and in some settings matches or exceeds oracle problem-level routing on math and coding.
thesis_use: baseline pattern (oracle routing as reference); text domain.

title: RESCUE: Is This Alarm Worth Acting On? Counterfactual Evaluation of VLA Runtime Monitors
relevance_note: MED — evaluates monitors by the value of the intervention, not detection accuracy (manipulation).
what: Restores simulator and policy states at checkpoints and compares alternative actions across 128,340 counterfactual branches with OpenVLA-OFT and pi_0.5 on LIBERO. Under the stop-and-reset model, even an idealised detector can afford only a 2.0-3.3% false-alarm rate before resets outweigh savings.
thesis_use: evaluation idea for the inspect/replan phase (judge a trigger by downstream cost, as the oracle-gain labels already do).

title: OccludeBench: Can VLMs Find What's Missing?
relevance_note: MED — occlusion benchmark for VLMs (not driving); VLMs recover hidden objects poorly.
what: Manually curated benchmark of fully occluded objects, direct (shadow/reflection cue) vs inferential. Across five VLMs accuracy averages 42.7% direct vs 62.7% inferential (20.0-point gap); humans 63.4% vs 68.5%. Extended reasoning and tool use give inconsistent gains; an inpaint-then-confront prompt reduces the gap.
thesis_use: supporting evidence that VLM prompting alone is weak on occlusion; motivates tool calls.

title: When to Ask for Help: A Decision-Theoretic Account and Measurement Standard for Slow-Module Scheduling in Dual-System Vision-Language-Action Models
relevance_note: MED — formal "whether to invoke an expensive module" objective with cost ratio, but manipulation (LIBERO).
what: Casts slow-module invocation as a calibrated decision problem with a Value of Intervention (VoI) quantity that covers fixed-ratio, fixed-budget and history-gated schedules as special cases. Measured systems span three orders of magnitude in cost ratio rho. Calibrated gains vanish under homogeneous collapse and grow with heterogeneity. A leak-free protocol cuts apparent early-warning AUC from 0.93 to 0.62 on 929 deployment traces.
thesis_use: framing and citation for "query value vs. budget"; idea to borrow (report cost ratio, leak-free evaluation of triggers).

title: Policy-Aligned Predictive Verification for Adaptive VLA Action-Chunk Execution
relevance_note: MED — learned verifier decides how much of a candidate plan to trust, reported as success-query trade-off (manipulation, not driving).

thesis_use: idea to borrow (evaluate candidates, plot accuracy vs. query cost); cite alongside TUD.

title: Agents' Last Doubt: Knowing When to Act and When to Step Back in Tool-Using Agents
relevance_note: MED — counterfactual outcome dataset over every legal action at each decision point (act, gather information, escalate), with a learned action-selection controller; accuracy vs interaction cost.
what: Builds 3,115 action outcomes from 1,036 decision points in ToolSandbox by executing each legal action; trains SURE-Act to select actions for a frozen backbone agent. Learning to rank beats a regression-only baseline by 0.0309 offline utility; end-to-end gains of up to 0.0575 (abstract truncated in my read).
thesis_use: idea to borrow (execute every candidate query to build counterfactual labels, rank rather than regress); same labeling recipe as our noise-averaged expected-gain targets.

title: Expand-and-Prune: Test-Time Candidate-Space Adaptation for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — candidate-set planners where uncertainty in trajectory scores sets a per-scene candidate budget.
what: Test-time framework that expands the native candidate set with intent-guided and temporal candidates, then prunes adaptively using uncertainty in intermediate trajectory scores. Improves four candidate-based planners on four benchmarks; LangAuto Driving Score 68.2 to 75.9; 72.5% of selected trajectories come from the new candidates.
thesis_use: related work on candidate-set-level adaptation under a budget; contrast with query (tool) budget. Idea: candidate-score uncertainty as a selector feature.

title: Perceives but Doesn't Brake: A Perception-Action Binding Gap in Reasoning Driving VLAs
relevance_note: MED — shows hazards are encoded but weakly control the plan; hazard-conditioned guidance in a frozen sampler (Alpamayo-1.5).

thesis_use: caveat / motivation: exact geometry (like a collision-check tool) helps when the planner can use it.

title: Post-hoc Epistemic Uncertainty for Vision-Language-Action Policies
relevance_note: MED — uncertainty from embeddings of one policy, used to decide referral to a stronger supervisor (accuracy-vs-assistance).

thesis_use: baseline-style uncertainty trigger computed from frozen embeddings; fits the "scene-uncertainty" selector family.

title: Model-Aware Generation of Safety-Critical Scenes for Robust End-to-End Driving via Distilled Planner Surrogates

thesis_use: motivation caveat (perception tools only help if planning can use them; same message as 2610.28184) and a hazard-scene generator idea for the benchmark. Not about tool selection.

title: Structured Representation Probing for Risk Anticipation in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
relevance_note: MED — learned runtime risk monitor on frozen driving policies; a signal that could feed an accept/inspect/replan policy.
what: Structured Representation Probe reads actor, ego and map representations from a frozen policy with linear risk directions and pooled scores. On Bench2Drive with DriveTransformer, UniAD and VAD it beats runtime baselines. On DriveTransformer at a 2 s horizon, ROC-AUC is 0.833 versus 0.715 for temporal consistency, with 2.67% readout overhead.
thesis_use: future-phase trigger or risk signal; baseline for "scene-level risk" selectors.

relevance_note: MED — information-seeking versus execution in driving under ambiguity, but classical MPC with no tools or VLM.

Over 5,000 simulations in lane-merging and unsignalized intersections, it reports the highest success rates (94.6% and 93.2%) and lowest collision rates (1.2% and 1.4%) among compared methods.
